title: Tim Schafer says Double Fine's unique games can be commercial hits if they can find their audience
text:
The Double Fine head says the studio was not profitable under Xbox.
Tim Schafer, the head of Double Fine Productions, says the studio hasn't tried to develop a game that it thought wouldn't be commercially viable.
Speaking to Bloomberg , Schafer provides insight about the studio's tenure under Xbox right until it was jettisoned at the start of July during the company's restructuring plan. Double Fine's newest titles, Keeper and Kiln , weren't a commercial success, and the studio wasn't profitable. Schafer said this unprofitability may have made some view Double Fine's output as prestige "arthouse" work—but he pushed back on that point of view, arguing there is market appeal for the team's catalogue
"We never actively tried to make a game we thought was going to lose money," Schafer tells Bloomberg. "I think people would say, 'oh, Keeper looks like this art house thing that no one expects to be a hit.' But to me it's the kind of game that someone who doesn't play games would love. I really think there's a mass market appeal to Keeper . If we could just get to those people, we could have them catch Lighthouse Fever."
Related: Planet Zoo maker Frontier Developments' adjusted operating profit jumps 62 percent
The expectations under Xbox changed at the beginning of this year when previous Xbox boss Phil Spencer retired and was replaced by Asha Sharma. "We had a mutually beneficial mission, which is just to put great games on Game Pass, and then their mission changed," Schafer says. "I can't imagine any amount of profitability—unless we had a breakout, Minecraft hit that year—would've saved us."
Double Fine regaining its independence was seen as a positive move, but this wasn't without cost. At the end of July, the studio laid off 23 staff members . "As a small, tightly-knit team, these actions are not taken lightly," Schafer said in a statement at the time. "Only the survival of our studio would ever make us consider such a painful action. Our transition to becoming an independent company also means becoming a size that we can sustain."
Now, the studio is running a Kickstarter campaign intended to fund the studio's own game jam, Amnesia Fortnight. Then, the winner of the jam will be polished up to become a small game published under Double Fine Action Labs, a "new label for weird little games." At the time of writing, the campaign has way surpassed its $400,000 goal with over 20 days left to go.
As Bloomberg reports, Double Fine is exploring other ways to generate revenue, such as ports and remasters, while Schafer pitches new games to potential investors. Whatever the next game might be, it sounds like it will retain the Double Fine signature, regardless of how it eventually does when it's out in the market.
Related: Trump Administration takes down Tetris clone after company warns it takes copyright violation 'very seriously'
"After all these years, how little I understand about the business just shows how hard it is to know," Schafer tells Bloomberg. "That's why I'm focused on keeping my team alive. That's why we do these creative things all the time. If we stopped doing these wacky creative things, we'd eventually be like, 'Who cares?' These games aren't lucrative enough to make up for how hard they are. They have to also be really fun and rewarding to make."

title: Report: EA is using genAI for commentator voiceover in NHL 27
text:
Veteran sports commentator John Buccigross claims EA showed him the tech using his voice for in-game commentary in NHL 27.
Veteran spots commentator John Buccigross claims that EA Sports is using generative AI (genAI) to create voiceover for in-game commentary in professional hockey simulator NHL 27 .
As reported by IGN (and first spotted by Insider Gaming executive editor Mike Straw), Buccigross told the Chirpin Zebras podcast about his participation in the game. This also led to him mentioning that EA is using genAI, as per an alleged demonstration.
"They're using some AI now; they played me some stuff back of my voice," Buccigross says on the podcast. "It's like 'wow, that's pretty good!' If that means less work but the same check, I'll take it."
The commentator adds that sometimes "AI will get something wrong," referencing an example during the alleged presentation. At one point while playing back his AI voice, it said "Score! And the crowd gets out of the chairs!", to which Buccigross said that they're called seats instead.
Related: Planet Zoo maker Frontier Developments' adjusted operating profit jumps 62 percent
"So, little things like that, you gotta go back and listen because words matter. [...] But then you can make AI smarter; in the future they'll say seats, they won't say chairs. You have to manually put that in. That was kind of a funny anecdote from the process," he says.
GenAI has garnered a largely negative reception from developers in recent years, with many arguing that it is having a corrosive effect on the industry. EA boss Andrew Wilson, on the other hand, has been adamant about his positive outlook on the tech. Back in 2024, he said that 60 percent of development processes could be "impacted by generative AI," adding that the tech is one the publisher was "embracing deeply."
Later that year, he reinforced the sentiment to investors, claiming genAI is at the " very core " of EA's business and that it's far from a "buzzword." In late 2025, EA partnered with Stability AI to co-develop AI models, tools, and workflows, claiming that this would empower its development teams to "reimagine how content is built."
Buccigross might seemingly be okay with his voice being allegedly replicated by artificial intelligence, but it's unsure whether EA is using the tech in other aspects of the game as well.
Game Developer has contacted EA for clarification on the matter.

title: Riot Games is considering making premium titles, says co-founder
text:
'Not every game needs to be infinite.'
As Riot Games moves on from its decision to end development on the fighting game 2XKO , developers and industry professionals have had plenty of reason to speculate about how the League of Legends and Valorant developer is strategizing for the future . At PAX West, chief product officer Marc Merrill teased a few elements of the company's future games during a fireside chat commemorating the company's 20-year anniversary. He described the Tencent-owned company's pursuit of a massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) as " the Grail ." But sharp-eared attendees viewers might have heard him mention another idea being considered at the free-to-play powerhouse: making premium, non-free-to-play games.
Merrill shared the news in an aside explaining Riot's philosophy for developing new games, saying that there's "no strategic imperative" that every game from the company has to be free-to-play. "We're working on some stuff that isn't [free-to-play]," he said, adding that whatever business model the studio lands on, it has to fit the vision of the game.
Related: Planet Zoo maker Frontier Developments' adjusted operating profit jumps 62 percent
Such a game would be unusual for Riot, which built its war chest on the back of a library of free-to-play games like League and Valorant that monetize by selling deeply invested players an ever-expanding coterie of cosmetics. Though the strategy is common now, Merrill recalled that when he and co-founder Brandon Beck sought funding for the studio before its launch in 2006, publishers and venture capital firms told them that making a free game was "the dumbest thing" they'd ever heard.
If Riot's biggest wins have been in the free-to-play realm, why would the company consider returning to the single-purchase premium model? In a follow-up interview with Merrill after the panel, the co-founder elaborated on those comments, saying "not every game needs to be infinite."
"Free-to-play tends to work really well with long-term engaging games... with optional cosmetics where people play for a long period of time," he said. "In many other game types, it creates these sorts of challenges from a design standpoint that can impact the integrity of the experience."
But the free-to-play market has become exceptionally challenging, as evidenced by the fate of 2XKO . In describing that game's failure to connect with a large audience, Merrill said that unless developers make something "incredible," they face stiff competition not just from the hundreds of other games launching on a weekly basis, but the near-infinite amount of content on social media fighting for their attention .
Related: Trump Administration takes down Tetris clone after company warns it takes copyright violation 'very seriously'
"We're competing for people's attention and time. That's a really high bar, and you have to get so many things right to get enough critical mass to build the [game's] community and have it turn into something sustainable in the long-term," he said in the panel. " 2XKO unfortunately didn't do that. That doesn't mean it's not a great game... that's why we're keeping the game live."
How would new premium games be different than those published by Riot Forge?
Riot technically isn't new to the world of premium games. It published a number of premium titles under the Riot Forge publishing banner—but wound down that initiative in 2024 in a move that also saw the company lay off 530 employees. However those games weren't made by Riot, but developed in partnership with studios like Digital Sun, Airship Syndicate, and Double Stallion.
What differentiates these potential new games from those made under Riot Forge? Merrill explained that Riot Forge was stood up to "go tell stories to acquire new customers."
"There's nothing wrong with that strategy from a macro standpoint, but as one example, one of the things that was really effective to acquire new players was Arcane," he said, referencing the 2021 Netflix show set in Runeterra, the fictional world of League of Legends . "The reason we did Arcane wasn't to go acquire new players. [It was] an outcome from doing something great."
Related: Report: EA is using genAI for commentator voiceover in NHL 27
He said that the company's view is that the world needs "things that are really excellent, really differentiating," because players already have an enormous amount of "content" to pick and choose from. He did seem to switch gears mid-sentence, stopping himself from describing what the world "doesn't need."
"We want to focus our efforts on those very-difficult-to achieve-things because we think, again, that the market does such a good job of meeting so many other needs."
In describing its planned MMORPG as "the Grail," Merrill certainly set a bar for what degree of difficulty Riot is willing to pursue in its future games. But while all eyes are on this title with ever-increasing expectations, it will be worth watching if smaller premium games become a major part of the League of Legends maker's strategy.

title: Blizzard union workers ratify historic contract covering 1,900 employees
text:
Union members have secured guardrails around generative AI usage, layoff protections, remote and hybrid work benefits, and more.
Employees at World of Warcraft and Overwatch developer Blizzard have ratified a historic union contract that includes guardrails around AI usage, layoff protections, and remote and hybrid work benefits.
Union members represented by the Communications Workers of America (CWA) claimed the new contract—which covers 1,900 employees across the Microsoft subsidiary—sets a new industry standard.
The union contract delivers wage increases, a three-day hybrid work week, remote working and disability accommodations, and grievance procedures. It also requires Microsoft to discuss, evaluate, and bargain over the usage of artificial intelligence in the workplace.
Notably, in an industry first, it also gives laid off workers the right to be "recalled" into open positions across any Blizzard bargaining unit within 14 months after their layoff was announced. An extra four weeks of severance for union workers has also been secured, irrespective of their tenure at the U.S. company.
Related: Strategically making Star Wars Zero Company, ft. Greg Foertsch
CWA president Claude Cummings, Jr. said Blizzard union workers are "leading the way" for all Xbox studios.
"It's a new day at Blizzard, where greater power for workers is translating into more innovative games for players," he added. "I am so proud of CWA bargaining teams, taking on tough fights and winning strong contracts that set new standards for working people across our industries."
The contract has been ratified days ahead of BlizzCon—Blizzard Entertainment’s flagship gaming convention in Anaheim, California. The news also comes shortly after Microsoft confirmed plans to eliminate 3,200 roles across Xbox before the end of the current fiscal year, starting with deep cuts at ZeniMax Online Studios, id Software, and Obsidian.
Microsoft has conducted five major rounds of layoffs within its video game division since acquiring Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion in 2023 .
Speaking to Game Developer in July , a number of workers impacted by the layoffs claimed major Xbox studios are being subjected to death by a thousand cuts. They also lambasted Microsoft for failing to treat those impacted with dignity and respect.
In a memo sent to staff ( and shared publicly ) in July, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said the division must "reset" after major bets on Xbox Game Pass and multiplatform releases failed to pay off.
The decision to carve through Xbox Game Studios has sparked widespread (and rather imaginative) protests from union members and supporters. CWA labor unions in Canada and the United States have also taken legal action against Microsoft for allegedly mishandling the layoffs.
Related: CD Projekt Red has The Witcher 4 running on all target platforms after Cyberpunk 2077 lesson
In a statement sent to Game Developer, Blizzard president Johanna Faries said the ratification of the contract represents a significant milestone for the studio.
"We appreciate the dedication and engagement of our represented employees and the bargaining committees throughout this process, as well as every Blizzard employee whose work continued alongside it," said Faries. "The ratification of these agreements marks a significant milestone and reflects our shared commitment to continuing to work together in support of our teams and our players."

title: Trump Administration takes down Tetris clone after company warns it takes copyright violation 'very seriously'
text:
Build The Wall has been knocked down.
The Trump administration's promise to promote its domestic and foreign policy agendas using video game iconography seems to have hit hit an (L-shaped) speed bump. On September 4, 2026, the White House added a new "Arcade" section to its website with five browser games themed around different policy pushes, each mechanically similar to existing games like Snake , Flappy Bird , and Tetris .
Now news outlet VGC has spotted that one of those games, a Tetris clone called Build the Wall , has already been taken down. The game in question was themed around President Trump's decade-long push for a physical border wall along the US' southern border that would forcibly block undocumented immigration.
This removal took place days after the Tetris copyright holder The Tetris Company posted a message on social media disavowing the game and promising that it takes copyright infringement "very seriously."
"At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," the company stated. "To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."
Related: Planet Zoo maker Frontier Developments' adjusted operating profit jumps 62 percent
It was in the comments of this post—also dated on September 4—that the company directly commented on Build the Wall . "P.S. The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of Build the Wall ," it continued. "P.P.S. We take copyright infringement very seriously." The Tetris Company is the first video game industry company to directly criticize the Trump administration's use of its intellectual property in its propaganda—and see its iconography removed in the days after.
Previous social media posts featuring iconography from games like Pokémon or Halo were met with either pointed distancing or silence by their property owners. The administration has faced sharper criticism by artists and companies in other mediums, with musicians like Taylor Swift and Bad Bunny successfully pressing for their songs to be removed from posts promoting its deportation agenda.
It's unknown at this time if The Tetris Company's post—or any follow-up messages to the White House by the Tetris Company—were what prompted the game's removal. A Tetris spokesperson declined to comment when contacted by Game Developer.
Build the Wall and Snake clone Rio Run were criticized as promoting racist depictions of undocumented immigrants from Central and South America. In Rio Run , players maneuver an anonymous government official across a board, gathering non-white characters that are placed in orange jumpsuits that become the "tail" of the digital snake.
Related: Riot Games is considering making premium titles, says co-founder
Meanwhile Build the Wall modified Tetris ' core mechanics by adding alien invaders that attempt to breach the assembled falling blocks. These otherworldly enemies are linked to the Trump administration's aggressive—often violent —deportation campaign by way of the term "alien," which the Immigration and Nationality Act defines as "any person not a citizen or national of the United States." The administration regularly refers to undocumented immigrants as "illegal aliens."
Ironically it may have been Build the Wall 's own design logic that undermined its intended message. As Kotaku observed before the game was taken down, Build the Wall removed the typical Tetris mechanic of having the falling blocks vanish when assembled in a perfect straight line, but still flashes a "game over" screen after the bricks reach the top of the screen.
In other words, no matter how high players built the wall, it was impossible to win.
Update 9/9: This story has been updated to include information on The Tetris Company's response to our request for comment.

title: August’s top grossing mobile games: Honor of Kings, Gossip Harbor, PUBG, Royal Match, Roblox, more
text:
Here are last month’s top grossing mobile games based on in-app purchase earnings, according to  Appmagic  data.
These IAP estimates do not include ad revenue, web shop spend, Apple and Google’s 30% cut or revenue from China’s Android ecosystem.
There’s commentary on which way the biggest earners are trending, and other interesting tidbits from the top 20 and beyond below.
In between these monthly updates, you can keep tabs on  Appmagic’s top grossing and top downloads charts anytime here .
Honor of Kings is back earning over $150m a month after a wobble in June, and is once again way ahead of the chasing pack which is led by Gossip Harbor for the first time.
AppMagic’s estimates suggest Microfun’s merge puzzler pulled in over $112m in IAP revenue last month, its best-ever performance, even after its steady growth dipped a little from April to June.
All of the top five earners in August broke the $100m barrier in August, with PUBG Mobile and Royal Match growing a little month-on-month to leapfrog Roblox , which dipped slightly.
In sixth spot, Whiteout Survival has now declined for the fifth month running, dropping steadily from March’s IAP earnings of nearly $115m to about $97m last month.
Scopely’s Monopoly Go had its best month of IAP revenue since January, though it’s still way down on the $110-130m it was pulling in the latter half of 2025. As ever, though, August’s IAP total of $95m doesn’t include all the players going through the game’s webshop.
Candy Crush Saga is recovering from a sudden dip in IAP revenue in June; King’s flagship puzzler earned about $86m from IAPs last month, but that’s down from the $95m-ish it was earning for most of the first half of 2026.
Century’s other hit game Kingshot is remarkably steady, and has posted IAP earnings of just under $80m for the third month running. The revenue graph for Konami’s eFootball is very spiky, though. It’s down to $58m for August after posting a record $69m the previous month, when it was the biggest beneficiary of World Cup fever.
August’s top grossing mobile games: 11-20
11. LastWar (Funfly): $56.7m
12. Delta Force (Tencent): $51.1m
13. Coin Master (Moon Active): $50.3m
14. Pokémon Go (Scopely Explore): $50.2m
15. Township (Playrix): $42.6m
16. Fate/Grand Order (Aniplex): $40.4m
17. Gardenscapes (Playrix): $40.3m
18. Royal Kingdom (Dream): $38.9m
19. Free Fire Max (Garena): $38.3m
20. Valorant Mobile (Tencent): $37.6m
LastWar ’s remarkable fall from the top earners bracket continued last month – the nearly $57m earned last month from IAPs is its worst performance since February 2024, back when it was still new and scaling up. That’s quite a drop from the $130-150m is was earning every month from September 2024 through to march this year.
Delta Force broke the $50m barrier again last month, while Coin Master’s gentle decline continues.
After its 10th anniversary celebrations in July, Pokémon Go ’s IAP earnings effectively halved for August and are back down to a more typical $50m-ish.
Japanese players suddenly started spending big again in longtime top grosser Fate/Grand Order , pushing it up 31 places month on month to hit 16th spot. And as we noted in data digest last week, Tencent’s China-only version of Valorant is dong really well; it pulled in nearly $38m last month from iOS players in China alone.
Outside the top 20, Pokémon TCG Pocket leapt up the rankings by 12 places, hitting nearly $30m in IAP revenue last month, while QualiArts’ Hololive Dreams continues to gather pace, up 14 places to hit nearly $29m in IAP revenue for August.
And after a revival of sorts last month, Hoyoverse’s trio of titles have all dropped in the rankings. Both Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail are down eight spots having earned around $24m and $23m respectively last month. Zenless Zone Zero slipped one place, racking up nearly $20m.

title: Data digest: Pokémon Go hits $9bn, Gameloft profits rise, GungHo sells $179m stake, fresh market stats, more
text:
Every Wednesday, we break down the latest data, research and financial results into digestible chunks. Read on for the numbers you need to know about without the fluff.
This column is sponsored by Xsolla , offering the #1 web shop solution for mobile games that generates more value, purchases, and revenue. Get started here .
Pokémon Go passes $9bn in lifetime revenue at its 10th anniversary
Pokémon Go has generated over $9bn in lifetime revenue and 800m downloads since launching in July 2016, according to Sensor Tower estimates.
The US leads on both – $3.6bn revenue and 145m downloads – while Japan ranks second in revenue at $2.4bn despite placing sixth in downloads (30m), giving it the highest revenue-per-download of any major market.
Gameloft posts $153.5m in H1 2026 revenue
Gameloft generated $153.5m (€132m) in revenue and $10.5m (€9m) in EBITA in H1 2026, up 10% year-on-year.
While 49% of revenue came via PC and console, its top five performers were all mobile titles: Disney Dreamlight Valley, Disney Magic Kingdoms, Disney Speedstorm, Asphalt Legends, and March of Empires.
Sony Music Japan buys stake in Puzzle & Dragons maker GungHo for around $179m
Sony Music Entertainment Japan is acquiring a 23.29% stake in GungHo Online Entertainment for ¥28.6bn (around $179m).
The deal – expected to close December 30 – makes SME GungHo’s largest shareholder. The two companies plan to explore joint game development across mobile, console and PC, potentially using Sony Music’s own IP. GungHo will remain independently listed.
Burlingame Studios secures $12m in UA financing
Burlingame Studios has secured $12m in non-dilutive user acquisition financing from PvX Partners, tied to the newly rebranded Flourish by Garden Joy (formerly Garden Joy). The studio, founded by veterans of CrowdStar, Glu Mobile, and EA, will use the funding to scale marketing without giving up equity.
Global games market forecast to hit $213.9bn in 2026
Newzoo forecasts the global games market will reach $213.9bn in 2026 , up 6.1% year-on-year, with growth across every region and platform.
Mobile remains the largest platform at $121.1bn, ahead of console ($46.9bn) and PC ($45.9bn). The global player base is expected to reach 3.7bn, up 4.4%.
Roblox creators added $752m to the US economy in 2025
Roblox creators contributed a $752m GDP impact to the US economy in 2025, up 69% from 2024, according to a new economic impact report.
Creators earned over $1.5bn globally in 2025, up from $923m in 2024, with 66% of US creator earnings ($444m) going to areas outside major tech hubs, part of what Roblox calls “decentralizing wealth outside of traditional tech hubs.”
Southeast Asia’s games market to pass $7bn by 2030
Niko Partners forecasts Southeast Asia’s SEA-6 games market (Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam) will grow from $5.6bn in 2025 to $7bn by 2030.
Indonesia leads by player count with 126m gamers, while Thailand is on track to pass $2bn in player spending this year.

title: 当90万玩家一起“突围”：一场从玩家到官方，从游戏到现实的公益接力
text:
今年6月26日，《暗区突围》端内上线了一个名为“突围吧少年”的公益捐赠活动。筹集的善款将用于残障青少年捐赠脑机接口仿生假肢。
那天，《暗区突围》联合腾讯公益、腾讯成长守护、四川省科技公益发展基金会，发起了“科技赋能助残行动”。玩家们可以直接在游戏中完成善款的捐赠。几个月后，这些善款变成了基于脑机接口技术的仿生智能假肢，捐赠给那些家庭经济困难的残障青少年。这些善款能够让一个先天失去手部功能的孩子，第一次拧开瓶盖，翻开书页；一个失去腿部功能的孩子可以从轮椅上站起，感受更自由的世界。
走出困境
久久公益节期间，《暗区突围》发布了这个项目的最新进展反馈。截至目前，已有31位受助人通过资料初筛和线下评估并完成取模，其中22位已经安装上了义肢，正在进行康复训练。按照项目节奏，后续的适配和安装仍将持续推进。
《暗区突围》这次的公益活动也给“突围”一词赋予了新的含义，它不再只是游戏中的一次撤离，更是帮助那些困难家庭突出生活重围的曙光。
“在卡莫纳，突围是撤离，是带出物资；在卡莫纳之外，突围是重新站起来，继续完成学业，是站上赛场，瞄准靶心，是推着轮椅走过河边的路。”
一个硬核战术射击游戏，为什么能快速集结起几十万玩家，走进现实中的公益事业？在我了解《暗区突围》的公益事业后，我发现这其实是一种《暗区突围》玩家自下而上的善意传递，这个故事可以从《暗区突围》主播小杰在今年2月发布的一条视频讲起。
■ 一条播放量最高的视频
小杰是《暗区突围》的头部主播，全网粉丝超过700万。在玩家眼里，他是游戏里“最会套包的主播”。但打开他的B站主页，播放量最高的一条视频却和《暗区突围》的游戏内容无关。那条视频的标题叫“特殊不该被定义”，记录了他今年2月回湖南老家做的一次线下公益，小杰自己联系了当地的特殊学校，走访困难家庭，捐出20万元的善款和物资。
这是小杰单笔投入最多的一次公益，也是他第一次真切地见到那些被公益帮助到的孩子们。
小杰是湖南永州人，出生在2006年，从小跟着爷爷奶奶在农村长大，过着类似留守儿童的生活，6岁那年才去广东深圳，到父母打工的地方上学。对弱势群体的共情，在他很小的时候就埋下了种子。村里有残疾的乡邻，他从小看到大，“心里面看了就很不舒服。”小杰说，“小时候没钱，路边看到乞讨的人，我也会把一块、五毛的零花钱捐出去。”
小杰来到特殊学校
主播事业做起来、经济逐渐独立之后，他开始在线上捐款：“月捐一直在弄，刷到自然灾害的视频也捐，像之前洪水，我每次下播之后，就直接会去捐一捐，几年下来累计至少也有五六万元。”线下公益的想法在心里放了很久，“能力越大，责任越大嘛，当时心里面就有一颗小种子，那种发芽的感觉。”直到去年年底，他觉得有了能力，也有了信心，趁着春节回老家，找到了这所特殊教育学校。
最开始，小杰打算只捐物资，并没有拍摄纪录片的计划。他说：“后面觉得如果能记录能分享出来，能让更多人注意到这群孩子，能号召更多人来关注，这才下了决心。”
因为是第一次做线下视频，想弄好一点，小杰还自费请了拍摄团队。拍摄算不上顺利，小杰在直播间以外的性格很内向，面对镜头容易紧张，介绍物资的时候一说话就结巴，只能一遍遍重来。
面对镜头介绍物资的小杰
但到了和这些特殊孩子们相处的部分，却很自然，一条都没有重来过。“到了现场最触动我的就是那些孩子们的纯粹。虽然这些特殊孩子条件有限，但是见到我，也会特别热情地打招呼，招手，主动过来跟我讲话。有的小孩不善言辞，但他们会把画的画塞到手里面。”小杰说，“那一刻我挺‘破防’的，比起物质，他们也需要被关照，被陪伴，被看见。”
开心的孩子们
在视频评论区里，玩家留下了大量支持的留言：“‘杰’出行动”，“小杰红温的甲，挡下的是孩子们被歧视的子弹啊”；视频下的最高赞评论则是《暗区突围》官方留下的：“感谢小杰点亮孩子们的成长之路，希望他们在今后的人生之路中向新“突围”，彩虹相伴。”可以说，《暗区突围》的公益氛围，甚至在官方行动之前，已经先从游戏生态内生长出来了。
实际上，在《暗区突围》的主播生态里，小杰不是第一个做公益的，也远不是唯一一个。
在2023年12月甘肃积石山地震后，主播中控王就向中国乡村发展基金会捐出1万余元，捐赠证书后来被晒在了《暗区突围》官方“暗区红人榜”的专访里。同时，中控王还长期拍视频记录自己的线下扶贫：2025年，他取出自己电竞馆开业头几天的全部营业利润，再自掏腰包添上一笔，去粮油市场采购米面油，送给县里的困难家庭。
这样的主播还有不少。“扶贫主播”梦求真在游戏里帮“仓库破产”的玩家翻身，在现实里也一户户走访困难家庭，他说自己从当上暗区主播的第一天起就在做慈善捐赠，这些年下来，还带动了不少主播一起加入。鸽哥多次为抗洪、震灾捐款捐物；战神特和一众暗区主播去过湖南常德石门县发过洪水的大山，为受灾居民带去问候和物资；染花香也在公益平台上为困境儿童医疗救助项目献过爱心。
对这些《暗区突围》创作者来说，做公益更像一种自然而然的事情，大家在有了一定能力之后，都愿意去帮助那些弱势群体，在代表《暗区突围》和粉丝的同时，也为数百万的粉丝们立下榜样，种下公益与向善的种子。
■ 90万人的24小时
在看到大量《暗区突围》玩家的善意后，游戏官方也很快就接住了这份善意。今年6月，《暗区突围》在涪陵落地了“暗区助学”，以卡莫纳人的名义为200名困境学生送上年度助学金（编者注：卡莫纳是《暗区突围》世界观里虚构的战乱国家，也是游戏对局的发生地，玩家社群中常用“卡莫纳人”代指暗区玩家。）；鸽哥、东东、鼠皇、梦求真四位主播也受邀走进乡村，与孩子们一起玩耍。
6月26日，“科技赋能助残行动”上线，目标是为符合适配条件的残障青少年免费捐赠仿生智能假肢。
把公益项目放在游戏中可以让更多玩家了解公益，参与公益
为了能让更多玩家参与公益，《暗区突围》在游戏内和小程序中开放了捐款入口，大量对公益抱有热情的玩家参与了这场捐款。24小时内，就达成了200万元的捐赠目标，有90万玩家涌入活动，其中8.5万人捐了不止一次。
在游戏的公开频道中，那些平日在战场上互不相让的玩家们，展现出了另一面，有玩家说：“这次谁愿意捐款呀？”“有那钱还不如自己用。”“搞得谁捐了一样。”而他们的共同点是——这些玩家ID右侧都挂着“突围·公益先锋”的小红花称号，这意味着他们都参与了这次公益捐款。
《暗区突围》游戏的小红花称号
《暗区突围》为这次公益活动设计的勋章也在鼓励这种氛围，这些献出爱心的玩家可以自豪地把自己献出爱心的记录永久留在自己的账号中，让公益的氛围传递在游戏中。同时，这次公益活动还新增了“随手捐”和“匿名捐”，即便那些没有《暗区突围》账号的人也可以参与公益，不难看出，官方有意让这场公益走出游戏，面向更多人。
不少从未在游戏里消费过的玩家，完成了“第一次爱心充值”；还有一些新玩家被这次出圈的公益活动吸引，注册账号，下载了游戏。就连新华社和央视网都跟进报道了《暗区突围》这次的公益行动。
新华社9月9日发布视频，报道《暗区突围》的公益行动
在《暗区突围》B站账号发布的公益视频《突围吧少年！微光汇聚，用爱照亮向新的路》的评论区当中，也有许多不玩游戏的观众对《暗区突围》的公益活动表达了赞许，有玩家留言：“我就捐1块，感觉好愧疚。”有人回复：“1元也是爱心啊！”玩家讨论的重心最终放在一起做了一件好事上，还有玩家感叹：“这是所有卡莫纳人最团结的一天。”
筹款目标达成后，玩家们的热情没有停下。4万多名玩家特意前往腾讯公益继续支持项目，留下了超过9999条留言，其中有玩家留言：“早日突围，走向希望的终点吧！”
许多《暗区突围》主播也参与了这次官方的公益活动：梦求真在直播里捐出9999元，说这是“一千零一份爱心……官方筹集一次，直接拿下”；战神特也在直播中带头捐款，他说：“主播有时候得起带头作用。”小杰在这次活动中捐了1万元。他说：“这次公益我感觉是非常难得的，从玩家的反馈就能够看出来，那种凝聚力，大家真心认可这种公益内容。很多玩家留言都说非常热爱这款游戏，愿意跟着官方一起去传递善意。就是能表达出，游戏能消遣娱乐，同样也可以承载现实的温度。”
■ 把做公益变成一件长期的事
把时间拉长看，这场助残行动并非孤例。自2024年起，《暗区突围》与腾讯成长守护围绕青少年成长的公益合作没有断过，几乎每年的久久公益节，暗区玩家都在参与一个新的项目。
公益向善
2024年9月，《暗区突围》第一次尝试用自己的号召力发动玩家做公益，加入了腾讯游戏的“爱心回礼”活动，支持“给孩子一堂科技课”项目。玩家的捐款变成了送到欠发达地区学校的“未来科技盒”：一套以组装并编程驱动智能小车为主线的科技教育套装。学生从认识电机、传感器与主控板入手，开展语音识别、视觉识别等人工智能应用实践。捐赠之外，项目还为乡村的科创老师提供培训和教学课件。
收到“未来科技盒”的孩子们
2025年9月，《暗区突围》与腾讯成长守护的合作延续到“给孩子一堂AI课”。这一年，腾讯成长守护把过去的“智体双百”计划扩大为“触梦计划”，公益范围从科技课扩展到运动、音乐、美术等领域，AI课是其中一项引入前沿科技的课程，为乡村孩子提供贴近素质教育的游戏化课程。
2026年1月，春节前，腾讯成长守护联合腾讯公益发起“新春游戏礼包捐”，《暗区突围》也参与其中，支持“童画车票守护成长”项目，帮助留守儿童在春节与外出务工的父母团聚。对很多暗区玩家来说，这个项目并不遥远——就像小杰的童年一样，公益项目帮助的孩子里，有许多玩家过去自己的影子。
《暗区突围》的公益项目为许多孩子带来爱与温暖。
到了2026年6月，《暗区突围》的公益事业再度加码，“突围吧少年”以卡莫纳人的名义为涪陵困境学生送上年度助学金，为他们提供生活补助、书籍物资和成长课程，而且官方明确表示，做公益将会持续下去。
“微光终成炬”
在“科技赋能助残行动”中，捐助给受助人的是BrainCo新一代智能仿生手高端版和轻凌智能仿生腿M3。仿生手可以通过解析神经电和肌肉电信号来识别使用者的运动意图，能控制到单根手指，可以做到单根手指的直觉控制，甚至连弹琴、打字这样的精细动作都做得到；仿生腿则依靠传感器实时采集数据，经算法处理后控制液压系统，随使用者当前的运动状态实时适配，让受助者可以像控制自己的腿一样，舒适、安全、自由地行走。
穿戴仿生腿的孩子在练习骑自行车
官方也明确表示，第一批义肢送达并非活动的结束，后续会继续反馈公益进展，直至全部义肢送达受助人手中并适配完成。游戏里持续更新着进度公示，目前已有受助人安装上了义肢，每期的公示末尾都写着同一句话：善款专款专用，进度实时公示，接受全体卡莫纳人监督。
回顾这些年《暗区突围》的公益事业，可以发现虽然形式与项目在变，从课堂到团聚，从助学到助残，但主题却有些类似——都是帮助青少年突破成长中的困境。围绕这件事，《暗区突围》把游戏做公益变成了一件长期主义的事情。
《暗区突围》游戏客户端内会向玩家公示当前公益项目的进度
长期主义也体现在项目的推进方式上，比如说助残项目的落地需要很长的周期，筹款达标之后，官方明确表示，第一批义肢送达并非活动的结束，后续会继续反馈公益进展，直至全部义肢送达受助人手中并适配完成。
某种意义上，这种做法带着游戏行业特有的产品思维，十分注重参与者的体验，对每一次善意给出反馈，玩家的每一次善意投入，也都会获得回响。
■ 让世界更美好
许多了解过公益事业的人都知道，比起去哪获得善款，一个公益项目最大的困难往往在于让更多人看见。大多数人都愿意帮助他人——帮到人的那一刻，成就感本身就是最高的奖励。
但在日常里，人们忙于工作和学业，很少有机会了解具体的受助项目。就算动了念头，也常常卡在找不到合适的项目，或者不确定哪家机构值得信任上。于是，许多善意就停在了想法上。
而游戏的场景恰好在某种程度上解决了这个问题，玩家每天打开游戏，在做日常任务或者领取奖励的时候，公益活动融入了游戏本身。大多数玩家也对自己每天游玩的游戏官方抱有信任，而且捐赠门槛低至1元，捐款流程也变得简单。
游戏的用户偏年轻，重荣誉感，社区表达轻松多样，做公益这件事在玩家之间传得又快又自然。当越来越多游戏开始做公益，真正能被记住的，是那些把自己所坚信的价值观、凝聚力和精神内核带进现实的游戏。
就像小杰说的那样：“公益对我来说肯定不是一次性的事情，我希望是长期的，细水长流的，能持续给到帮助的那种。”
更多的“突围”正在路上。

title: 触乐怪话：期待9月10日
text:
触乐怪话，每天胡侃和游戏有关的屁事、鬼事、新鲜事。
对的对的，就是这样！（图/小罗）
今天是9月9日，明天是9月10日。从前几天开始，有一个事情我一直在心里隐隐约约地存在，但是没有说出来，那就是我真的很期待9月10日。
这种期待不算特别正式，也很少被付诸口头纸面，有时候还比较隐私。比如，我可以坦坦荡荡地在一篇稿件里说“我期待某款产品给行业和品类带来新的启发”，但我确实似乎有点难为情公开告诉所有人：我其实特别期待9月10日，我想玩《王者万象棋》，也想赶紧在《王者荣耀》里买上返场的王昭君“映山客”皮肤，我还特别期待《夜幕之下》在这天开启某某人的新卡池……
为什么会觉得难为情？我觉得可能一定程度上是因为这些“期待”听起来都不太成熟，略有幼稚，也有点夸张——毕竟并不是模糊地期待，而是很具体地关注、等待、盼望着某个具体的日子，甚至会特意为了这个时间熬夜到0点或者凌晨4点。
其中还夹杂一些微妙的鄙视链：如果我说期待某款单机大作、期待某天堂直面会，好像也可以大方地在社交媒体分享；但非常期待某个手游的新皮肤、新卡池，则有一点……对吧，好像有点太容易开心、满足和幸福了，也不够志趣高雅。
但也就在昨天，我偶然刷到了一篇小红书的帖子。帖子的第一句话是“怎么还不到九月十号？”，我刷到的时候时间好像还早，发帖人只写了短短几行字：“星期四真是个好日子，《王者万象棋》开服，《洛克王国世界》新赛季，奇幻商店返场。”
这则帖子一开始被我点了赞后就略过了。它只是提醒了我，原来明天还有《洛克王国世界》新赛季，我要上线抓新的赛季精灵。但等到今天早上，我再刷到这篇帖子的时候，我发现它的点赞已经达到了3万，作者在帖子上补充了二编三编四编一直到十编，整个帖子变得密密麻麻，汇聚了各种各样的人所“期待”的事情，也不止于游戏。
密密麻麻
这种感觉很奇妙。各种各样的人的期待，有的可能才是真的对我来说已经很遥远、我从来没想过的期待，比如保研名单公布，盛香亭新品发布，某位明星新商务官宣，某条Lolita裙子开启补款……各种各样的来自某个人的期待，可能在某些时候看起来也有点幼稚吧？也不好意思明确或者公开地告诉不熟悉的人，但真的在日思夜想，掰着手指计算。翻看这条帖子的时候，我也想起了很多已经有点被我忘记了，但很确切地期待过的小事。
得益于这篇帖子的集思广益，我还发现9月10日要发生的、和游戏有关的事情真的很多，列出来的效果非常让人惊讶，包括：
《王者万象棋》开服。《倩女幽魂》重生服开服。易次元《问道长生》上线。
《洛克王国世界》新赛季。《第五人格》新赛季。《无限暖暖》新版本。《物华弥新》新版本。《中二节奏》2027大版本更新。《地铁跑酷》新赛季。《使命召唤》新赛季。《剑网3》联动《凡人修仙传》版本上线。《战双帕弥什》新版本前瞻。
《如鸢》和《代号鸢》新活动开启。《刀剑乱舞》花牌活动。《燕云十六声》捉迷藏新活动。《地下城与勇士》米歇尔团本上线。《冒险岛》怀旧服新联动活动开启。《金铲铲之战》“西部天使 幻想召唤”活动上新。
《鸣潮》新卡池。《时空中的绘旅人》新CR卡。《未定事件簿》左然新卡池。《心动小镇》蓝钻池和风物池开启。《白荆回廊》新卡池。
《无畏契约》乖狗狗套装。《逆水寒》新时装。《王者荣耀》奇幻商店皮肤开启。《QQ农场》新狗狗上市。《光遇》兔子徽章上线。《蛋仔派对》线条小狗联动皮肤返场。《超自然行动组》呆猫八条联动。《云顶之弈》免费第二次抽神话小小英雄活动开启。
《崩坏：星穹铁道》和大白兔奶糖的联动发售。《明日方舟》乌尔比安进店。《小花仙》更新。《皮卡堂》更新。
《世界之外》夏萧因生日。
这些被列出的游戏涵盖了当下流行的手游、端游，还有一些比较“古早”的页游等等。每款游戏的信息都来自评论区具体的玩家。我不太确定，也没有验证，是不是其实每天都会有很多很多的类似的事情，只是我没有注意到？但这种看着所有人都有“盼头”的感觉，确实也会觉得有一种更加觉得明天值得期待的感觉。
感觉日子一下子好起来了！
今年年初的时候，我写过一篇有关在《王者荣耀》里过年的稿件，稿件里采访了一些玩家，其中有几位玩家对我说“想到过年可以和朋友一起打王者，就感觉很幸福”“想到后天0点就可以上线换上新衣服，现在每天都日思夜想，什么事情也做不下去”“看到社群的讨论，会越看越期待”，我非常理解他们，因为我也有类似的感受。有时候我会觉得，人的期待是可以被叠加的，自己在期待某个时间的时候，能感受到别人也有类似的期待，便会觉得自己的期待似乎更有意义。而最常见的一个被集体期待和盼望的时候也就是过年了。以前我总感觉这样的被集体期待的日子很少，现在发现还是很多的嘛。

title: What To Expect From BlizzCon 2026: StarCraft’s Return, A Whole Lot Of Warcraft
text:
BlizzCon 2026 begins September 12, and while there is big news every time developer Blizzard decides to host its fan convention, after a two-year hiatus, this year's show in particular seems poised to be a major occasion for fans of Blizzard franchises like Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch.
Blizzard president Johanna Faries hasn't been shy about hyping up this year's show in interviews, calling 2026 Blizzard's "biggest year yet." She said its various development teams are "cooking on big swings" across its key franchises and that this year's BlizzCon will reflect the studio's goal of being the "best gaming and entertainment company in the world." BlizzCon's announcements will deliver the "heart and soul" of what fans want out of a BlizzCon, she said, while still "bringing some very new things to the table."
What, then, should fans expect from what is being billed as the biggest year in Blizzard history? Let's dive into what to expect from BlizzCon 2026, as well as a few predictions.
A Whole Lot Of Warcraft
For years, BlizzCon essentially served as a new World of Warcraft expansion vessel. Blizzard would get on stage, announce a new expansion with a jaw-dropping cinematic, and then dive into all the details of the new expansion.
That will still likely happen this year, though we do already know the name and setting of WoW's next expansion, The Last Titan, since Blizzard announced an entire trilogy of expansions back at BlizzCon 2023. The reveal of the expansion's cinematic and more details, including its revamp of Northrend, major new features, and possibly a release date, is a given. Expect to learn more about Midnight's 12.2 patch as well.
However, there's likely to be more Warcraft this year than perhaps any other time in Blizzard's history. In addition to The Last Titan, it's not exactly a secret that Blizzard is cooking up a new version of WoW Classic, unofficially called Classic+ by the community. What form this version of Classic will take is still unknown, but many fans expect it to serve almost as an alternate timeline for WoW where the game didn't release new expansions every few years and instead turned its focus to the core regions of Azeroth fans were already familiar with. That could mean Blizzard finishing or expanding zones from original WoW, class redesigns, additional endgame content, or even new playable races and classes.
Dataminers discovered a reference to a new build for Classic called "Camelot" within Blizzard's files earlier this year. That codename at first glance didn't mean much but was quickly connected to a once-dismissed Warcraft release slate leak from last year that mentioned Camelot by name.
That connection suddenly made the leak much more credible overall, and it shows Camelot could possibly release this year shortly after BlizzCon. This, of course, wouldn't be out of the ordinary for WoW Classic. The game's previous experiment that many saw as a testing ground for Classic+, Season of Discovery, was announced at BlizzCon 2023 in early November and was then released only a few weeks later. It certainly seems like history could repeat for Classic+, Camelot, or whatever Blizzard officially calls it.
But Classic+ is far from the only new Warcraft project included on the alleged leaked release slate. According to the alleged leak, Blizzard may also be making a new Warcraft RTS titled Warcraft Chronicles for 2027, as well as an Arthas RPG spin-off for 2028.
Those would be huge news on their own, but beyond games, the leak additionally lists a tie-in television show for each game. The idea of Blizzard working on television shows isn't as far-fetched as it sounds. Faries said in an interview earlier this year Blizzard has had "exciting conversations" about Hollywood adaptations of its IP, while Blizzard VP and executive producer for WoW Holly Longdale has been on record that the Warcraft IP is "underutilized" and that Blizzard wants to expand it beyond just WoW.
It's possible the leaked slate is years old and no longer accurate (or just an extremely coincidental fake), but it wouldn't be surprising if all of what it detailed and more appeared at BlizzCon.
StarCraft Is Back In A Big Way
StarCraft has been a largely dormant franchise for close to a decade. The last major DLC for StarCraft 2 released in 2017, the same year StarCraft: Remastered released. Since then, Blizzard's sci-fi franchise has been relegated to cosmetic crossovers in other Blizzard games like Diablo 4 and Hearthstone.
That looks to be finally changing at BlizzCon this year. Persistent reports have indicated Blizzard is working on a StarCraft shooter of some kind, though additional details on what kind have been scarce. There are also reports Blizzard is partnering with Korean video game giant Nexon for a licensing deal that could potentially see Nexon develop new StarCraft games.
At least one new StarCraft title getting revealed at BlizzCon this year seems like a certainty, though it's possible Blizzard also officially announces its partnership with Nexon as well.
Blizzard is sending clear signals that something is happening on the StarCraft front . The website for StarCraft: Remastered recently started "glitching" out, perhaps serving as a not so subtle nod that news is on the way. Those "glitches" have revealed secret transmissions and bits of new lore that look to be setting the stage for Blizzard's shooter.
Fans are theorizing the game could be a PvE co-op shooter in the vein of Helldivers 2, where a team of players land on an abandoned lunar mining facility overrun by Zerg, have to complete objectives, and then extract. Or it could be the triumphant return of StarCraft: Ghosts, though my money would be on the PvE co-op shooter. Regardless, StarCraft will almost certainly make a return at this year's BlizzCon, though its new form may disappoint RTS fans.
Diablo New And Old
What Blizzard is cooking up on the Diablo front is largely a mystery. It is, however, Diablo's 30th anniversary, so it seems safe to bet Blizzard will be announcing big news about the franchise at the show. A Diablo 30th anniversary presentation earlier this year concluded with Blizzard teasing a major BlizzCon announcement, stating "they are going to freak out at BlizzCon when we announce" a moment before the end of the broadcast.
Alongside a Switch 2 port of Diablo 4 , the announcement of a new Diablo 4 expansion, alongside a reveal cinematic, is almost a given. Blizzard once pledged yearly expansions for Diablo 4. That didn't come to pass, but the gap between the game's Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred expansion's was faster than Diablo fans are used to, with a little over a year and a half between them. With Lord of Hatred having been released back in April, a new expansion in the back half of 2027 seems plausible.
Blizzard certainly has no shortage of villains to choose from, with Diablo himself having still failed to make an appearance in Diablo 4. The return of Malthael could also be in the cards, with the game's latest season making multiple not so subtle references to the fallen angel. Aside from a new expansion, Blizzard has already promised more details and surprises related to Season 15.
Of course, Diablo as a franchise is bigger than Diablo 4. Earlier this year, Diablo 2: Resurrected received new content in the form of the Reign of the Warlock DLC , adding a new class and some long-requested quality-of-life features to the classic ARPG. There's also Diablo Immortal, the ongoing mobile game Blizzard co-operates with NetEase.
A quick look at the BlizzCon schedule reveals there sure is a lot of time dedicated to a Diablo Immortal "event" across both days of the show, something fans are finding suspicious. It would certainly be bold of Blizzard to dedicate so much time and space to the game that led to the most memed moment in BlizzCon history, the infamous "do you guys not have phones?" moment from Diablo Immortal's reveal Q&A during BlizzCon 2018. That fact has led some fans to speculate that surely there must be something else related to Diablo coming that will take up more of that timeblock. The real question is what.
It wouldn't be surprising if Blizzard announced a new Diablo 2 expansion. The demand clearly seems to be there given the reception to Reign of the Warlock, and there are still plenty of Diablo fans who view D2 as the pinnacle of the series in much the same way WoW Classic fans put vanilla WoW above all subsequent versions. Given it's the franchise's 30th anniversary, a potential remake of the original Diablo also seems like a possibility, though what form that might take is more uncertain.
Overwatch Keeps Its Momentum
Overwatch has had a big year so far, with Blizzard essentially rebooting its hero shooter by dropping the "2" from its name , putting an emphasis on year-long storylines, and adding more playable heroes this year than ever before. The game added five new heroes at once earlier this year, and has continued to add a new hero every season since.
Going into BlizzCon 2026, I expect Blizzard to keep that momentum going into next year. By abandoning Overwatch 2's promised PvE story missions back in 2024 and even ceasing new content development for the game's newest game mode, Stadium , Blizzard looks to be focusing on what works and cutting out what doesn't. That's resulting in more events, cosmetics, crossovers, and heroes faster than ever, and Blizzard is no doubt putting more resources into ensuring that gravy train continues.
As for what that means for BlizzCon, expect new map reveals and plenty of new hero announcements. Blizzard hasn't yet revealed the game's next hero coming as part of Season 5, so that's a shoo-in. There's a good chance a hero trial for the Season 5 hero goes live during BlizzCon, as was the case with Mauga's reveal at BlizzCon 2023. Season 6's new hero, and heroes even beyond that, will likely be revealed as well. Though Blizzard initially only promised a new hero for each 2026 season, I would be shocked if the new hero per season status quo doesn't continue into 2027.
BlizzCon will also likely set the stage for the finale of Overwatch's 2026 storyline, The Reign of Talon. Story has been a big focus for Overwatch this year, with plenty of comics, short stories, and animations propelling the game's narrative forward. In addition to getting a good look at how 2026's storyline will conclude, I expect to learn where the story will be going next, too, with Blizzard possibly announcing the name and theme of 2027's seasonal story arc.
One big question is whether Blizzard reveals a new core Overwatch game mode. Blizzard's track record hasn't been great on this front. Clash, added in 2024, hasn't been popular and was removed from both competitive and quickplay. Stadium was added last year, but its low player count saw Blizzard recently announce it was putting the mode on life support . I would be surprised then if Blizzard attempts to throw another new mode at the wall and see if it sticks so soon after Stadium's failure, as it seems like its resources would be better spent elsewhere.
Rather than announcing a brand new mode, Blizzard may instead put more emphasis on 6v6. It's no secret Blizzard has been experimenting more and more with 6v6 in recent months. While I don't expect 5v5 to vanish, the introduction of a proper, permanent role queue for 6v6 seems like a real possibility.
Whatever Blizzard is cooking across its franchises, fans won't have to wait long to learn what's in store. BlizzCon's opening ceremony begins September 12 at 10:30 AM PT / 1:30 PM ET.

title: GameStop Sets A New Financial Record, And It’s No Thanks To Games
text:
Retailer GameStop has released its latest earnings report , and it was a record-breaker for the company. The Texas-based retailer's biggest number for its fiscal Q2 quarter that ended August 1 was $160.2 million. That's how much GameStop made in operating income for the period, and it was the highest Q2 operating income level since the company went public in 2002.
Net income was up, too, reaching $298.7 million, compared to $168.6 million last year.
GameStop benefitted from continued growth in its biggest sales category--collectibles--which saw net sales jump a whopping 57% year-over-year to $356.3 million. For this latest period, collectibles made up 45.1% of GameStop's net sales.
GameStop was once primarily known as a video game retailer, and while it still sells games, consoles, and accessories, the company's biggest revenue-driver today is collectibles. Anyone who has walked into a GameStop store recently can attest to how much shelf space is dedicated to collectibles.
GameStop's next-largest revenue-driver was its "video game" category, which reached $263.2 million for the period, down sharply from $494.6 million during the same period last year that benefitted from the Switch 2 launch. Finally, GameStop's pre-owned and refurbished business made up $170.7 million during the period, down from $250 million last year.
Some might have thought that Sony's decision to end support for physical game discs, and GTA 6 not releasing on a disc, would be a death knell for a company like GameStop. However, physical video game sales are "irrelevant" to the company , CEO Ryan Cohen has said. He has also suggested GameStop could expand its business into the "live commerce" category that is popular on TikTok . The executive has also discussed the possibility of GameStop becoming a marketplace for re-selling digital gaming items .
While GameStop's operating profit jumped, net sales for the company overall fell from $972.2 million in Q2 last year to $790.2 million this year. GameStop said the decreases was primarily attributable to the launch of the Switch 2 last June, an event that benefitted GameStop. The downturn in overall revenue was also attributable to store closures and GameStop getting out of its business operations in France, the company said. GameStop's share price tumbled after the report came out.
GameStop also scaled back selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) costs during Q2 this year, with those expenses reaching $187.1 million, compared to $218.8 million during the same period last year.
GameStop is forecasting even rosier times ahead, projecting $650 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) for its fiscal year ending January 30, 2027. That's up from a previous forecast of adjusted EBITDA of $600 million.
In another move, GameStop is trying to buy the auction site eBay, but so far, its proposals have been rejected buy eBay's board. GameStop owns more than 43 eBay shares, worth about $4.9 billion today.

title: Xbox’s Disc-To-Digital Program Has A Big Problem: Several Major Publishers Aren’t Participating
text:
Xbox's disc-to-digital program looks like it could be a vital step forward for players who want to hold on to their physical games in an increasingly digital world, but it does have limits. Not every game publisher is on board with it, it seems, as Xbox users are reporting that four of the biggest companies aren't "participating" at all.
So far, it looks like games from Sega, Square Enix, Ubisoft, and Bandai Namco are largely incompatible with the disc-to-digital service. As verified by Kotaku , popping in a disc for a game from one of those publishers could result in a "not participating in digital licensing" message. A fan effort to catalogue all the games that do work with it also shows which titles from those publishers are incompatible with disc-to-digital, so if you were holding on to a physical edition of Far Cry 4, Final Fantasy 15, or Dark Souls 3, you're out of luck.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s
This could be rectified in the future if those publishers decide to sign up--Xbox has mentioned that this will be a gradual rollout for the service--but the current wording of the message and the sheer number of games involved suggest otherwise. What's the reason for this? It could be down to good ol' economics, as the companies would probably prefer that you buy one of their games again on the digital storefront. After all, if you decide to pick up a physical copy of a title from a local secondhand store or through a private sale, they're not seeing a cent of that cash when it changes hands.
This is something that Square Enix has been called to task over, as several of its big HD-2D RPGs have no upgrade path to Switch 2 . For example, if you purchased Octopath Traveler for the Switch, there's no complimentary or premium upgrade pack to give it sharper graphics and new features on a Switch 2 console. Instead, you'll have to buy the game again when its Switch 2 version launches, and you don't even get an option to transfer your save game over.
All of this paints a worrying picture for game preservation, as Square Enix, Sega, Bandai Namco, and Ubisoft represent a sizable chunk of the gaming market with several big franchises and numerous smaller games spread between them. Microsoft may want to make the transition to an all-digital future easier --and better than Sony's plan to go all in on ditching physical media--but not every company wants to play ball.

title: Xbox Game Pass Adds A Great Call Of Duty Game Today
text:
Xbox Game Pass grows today with the addition of a popular Call of Duty game. New to the service from today, September 8, is 2020's Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War . It's available on Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, and PC Game Pass, and the game supports cloud streaming as well.
Developed by Treyarch and Raven, Black Ops Cold War is set in Cold War-era 1981, with its campaign following Russell Adler as he and his team seek out a spy named Perseus. The game also has multiplayer, of course, along with Zombies.
Black Ops Cold War was a bit hit, becoming 2020's best-selling game overall in the US .
Game Pass isn't done adding more titles this month , as The Royal Writ and Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O World Stage arrive on September 10, followed by RuneScape: Dragonwilds on September 15.
After Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard, many assumed that back-catalog Call of Duty games would flood Game Pass, but that didn't happen. Instead of releasing Call of Duty games en masse to Game Pass, Microsoft has taken more of a selective approach. Black Ops Cold War is now just the sixth Call of Duty game on Game Pass, joining Call of Duty: WWII, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and Black Ops 6.
Modern Warfare 3 and Black Ops 6 were released day-and-date into Game Pass, but that's ending this year, and any Game Pass subscriber who wants to play Modern Warfare 4 at launch this October will have to pay for it ... or wait a year.

title: Major Steam Leak Reveals Achievements For Persona 6, Kingdom Hearts 4, And Unannounced Games
text:
A massive Steam leak has revealed hundreds of achievements for upcoming games, including highly anticipated titles like Kingdom Hearts 4, Persona 6, and Fable. On the website Exophase--which tracks achievements for games on Steam, Epic Games Store, and more--the achievement lists for numerous in-development games were uploaded to it and made public. It looks like the site trackers scraped up all the achievements uploaded to Steam recently, resulting in potential story spoilers and the reveal of several unannounced--or canceled--titles.
"Seems like a possible screw-up on Valve's end, a bunch of games with achievements that should be private are accessible through the API right now, and that's why they got scanned into the site," Exosphere owner Mike Bendel AKA x3sphere wrote in a  ResetEra post . "I usually never see games without an actual name pop up with achievements, yet over the past hour or so, a bunch have (when there's an unknown name, we just set it to the AppID)."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3NrZKxdh6Q
It's worth noting that many of these achievement lists appear to be incomplete due to the use of placeholder text, but many of them are rife with spoilers. While we won't mention them here, the leak has revealed more of the Disney-themed worlds that players can travel to in Kingdom Hearts 4 , and story details for Persona 6 have surfaced. People are, of course, digging deep into the list, so if you're looking to go into any particular game without fear of spoilers, it might be time to start muting certain keywords before it's released.
This isn't the first time Steam has been responsible for leaking data. Last month, a security breach saw 13TB of information on unreleased games and prototypes uploaded to online spaces and made available for download. This leak covered games uploaded to Steam between 2003 and 2013, including pre-release builds of major games from the era, such as Spore, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and an early Portal 2 prototype.

title: Resident Evil Movie Director Reacts To Backlash, Says He Was “Naive” To Think Gamers Would Embrace Him
text:
One of the talking points surrounding the upcoming Resident Evil movie is that director Zach Cregger took an original idea and slapped the Resident Evil name on it. That's not true , Cregger has said, and now he's shared more of his thought process as it relates to some of the blowback from fans of the games.
He told IGN that, in retrospect, he feels it was "naive" to think that fans of the games would immediately embrace his pitch for his Resident Evil movie.
"I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration," he said. "I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?"
Cregger went on to say he hopes fans of the game see his movie "regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment" that he's not re-telling a story from the games. He said he hopes fans of the games "feel seen" when they watch the movie and see "all of the love for the games that are in this movie."
"This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love," he said.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNd1gb19A-c
In a separate interview with The Playlist , Cregger said the press tour he's doing to promote Resident Evil feels more like an "apology tour" given all the negative sentiment from fans. "I feel like I’m running for office, trying to get these people not to call me a LARPer," he said.
"Now, I’m just like, 'You know what? See the movie.' If you still feel the same way after you’ve seen it, then whatever you think is fair. You’re going to decide if I’m an actual Resident Evil fan or a fake. What can I say? I think the movie is going to speak for itself," he added.
Also in the interview, Cregger addressed the possibility of working on another Resident Evil movie project in the future. He said he "can't help" to think about "other places this story could go," adding that he has "ideas." At the same time, Cregger pointed out that his movie isn't even out yet. "Let's see what happens," he said.
In a different interview, Cregger said he's done with franchise movies and will only make original projects going forward . His next movie is The Flood, a sci-fi film set in space. Cregger previously directed Barbarian and Weapons.
Resident Evil releases in theaters on September 18, starring Austin Abrams as a medical courier who visits Raccoon City where all hell breaks loose .

title: Kingdom Hearts 4 Leak Reveals One Of Its Most Unexpected Worlds
text:
Today is not a good day to be hit with Kingdom Hearts 4 spoilers, as thanks to what appears to be a massive Steam leak , achievement lists for multiple games have appeared online. Amongst the games caught in the leak is Kingdom Hearts 4, and if the data is real, several of the game's worlds have been revealed early. So far, only the world of Pixar's Coco has been officially confirmed by Disney, but it looks like players might be visiting one of the biggest IP from the House of Mouse, for the first time ever. Consider yourselves warned, as there are potential spoilers below.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3NrZKxdh6Q&pp=ygUZZ2FtZXNwb3Qga2luZ2RvbSBoZWFydHMgNA%3D%3D
The various achievements uploaded to the achievement-tracking site Exophase mention various Disney worlds, but Star Wars is easily the biggest of them all. The iconic franchise has grown massively since Disney acquired it in 2012, expanding with a new sequel trilogy, spin-offs, and animated series. Which era of Star Wars could Sora visit? That's going to be the real surprise if and when Disney announces it.
This isn't the first time that Star Wars has been linked to Kingdom Hearts 4. Back in 2022 , a trailer for the game featured a quick glimpse of what appeared to be an All Terrain Scout Transport--the big mechanized troop-carriers from the iconic Hoth battle in The Empire Strikes Back--and the world that footage was taken from was a dead ringer for the forest moon of Endor, the home of the Ewoks.
Beyond Star Wars, the leaked achievements also listed the following worlds for Kingdom Hearts 4:
Haunted Mansion
Imagineer Planet
Galaxy Far, Far Away (Star Wars)
Land of the Dead (Coco)
Monochrome Origins
Quadratum
Savanna Central (Zootopia)
Scala ad Caelum
Toy Box (Toy Story)
That's a pretty safe selection of worlds for Kingdom Hearts 4, if the leak turns out to be accurate. Toy Story and Zootopia have been big box-office draws for Disney, Coco allows for an imaginative tour of the afterlife, and original worlds like Scala ad Caelum fit the bill for a Square Enix destination that has a weird name attached to it. Sadly, the list doesn't include worlds from other Disney IP, like It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, the Predator homeworld of Yautja Prime, or a hellhole infested with Xenomorphs. We're never going to see Frank get a Keyblade, are we?
While it has been a long time since a new installment in the Kingdom Hearts series was released, it looks like you won't need to wait much longer for this new chapter. Franchise co-creator Tetsuya Nomura recently spoke about the game at Disney's D23 Expo, promising that  Kingdom Hearts 4 will come out in 2027 . And who knows? We might even get a Kingdom Hearts movie one day.

title: AI Could “Kill All Humans” In Next Decade, Anthropic Lead Says
text:
Anthropic alignment science lead Evan Hubinger has said the AI company behind Claude and other AI products "earnestly" believes that AI "could kill all humans," and it could happen in the next decade.
Posting in response to Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon's own resignation from the company due to safety concerns , Hubinger said, "We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade."
He added: "I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to."
Hubinger, who still works at Anthropic, went on to cite Anthropic's own latest risk report that says the risk of AI wiping out humanity from present models is "low." However, Hubinger said he is worried that superintelligence could arise from "recursive self-improvement," which is the term for AI rewriting its own code and constantly improving itself.
For his part, Coxon said the AI market leaders Anthropic and OpenAI are not "acting responsibly" with regards to safety. "Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing," Coxon wrote.
He said Anthropic is pushing ahead despite these concerns because the company is "locked in a race to get there first." He said a company like OpenAI isn't taking the issue seriously enough but Anthropic understands the "civilizational stakes," and, if "no one else will act responsibly ... they must do it themselves, despite the risk."
Unsurprisingly, these posts have generated a lot of debate and discussion. Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont said , "AI threatens our economy, privacy, democracy and the well-being of our kids." He is lobbying Congress to "stand up to the big tech oligarchs and protect the American people."
Senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut, meanwhile, advocated for "a regulatory system that allows the research to continue, but in a way that doesn't destroy us."
https://twitter.com/ChrisMurphyCT/status/2097669346814304677
Veteran media and technology reporter Taylor Lorenz, meanwhile, said Hubinger's comments are "sanctimonious doomer" statements that may lead to "passing the worst laws imaginable." She called on Hubinger, if he truly believes AI systems could endanger society, to provide "actual proof and receipts."
"Otherwise you're just vagueposting and fomenting fear which will result in terrible policy," she said .
Another matter at play here is that Anthropic is expect to go public this year at an expected valuation of north of $2 trillion. Some have theorized that the "kill all humans" comments from Anthropic itself could be strategic move to create panic in the marketplace in a bid to follow the business strategy of "create the problem and then sell the solution." If Anthropic expects there to be AI regulation, the thinking goes that they could be the ones to help write the rules in ways that would benefit them. Anthropic boss Dario Amodei previous said AI could eliminate half of all entry-level white collar jobs in the coming years , comments that many took to be aimed at fundraising.
Whatever the case, AI business today is helping fuel the growing US economy, and many are expecting the bubble to burst, leading to big pain in the market. AI is a big topic in video games, too, and it was just recently revealed that EA Sports used generative AI to clone a commentator's voice . The use of AI and generative AI in video games has been controversial, with many expressing fears of numerous negative effects like job losses and heavier workloads.

title: Now You Can Play Star Fox Adventures On Switch 2 And Decide If It’s Terrible Or Great Yourself
text:
The black sheep of the Star Fox series, Star Fox Adventures, has landed on the Nintendo Switch Online service. As announced in the September 2026 Nintendo Direct , the GameCube title is available to play as a Nintendo Classic today for subscribers of Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack.
Star Fox Adventures came out in 2002 and marked a departure from the dog-fighting gameplay the series is known for. Developed by Rare, the game began life as Dinosaur Planet for Nintendo 64 before Shigeru Miyamoto proposed converting it into a Star Fox game.
Featuring Zelda-like action-adventure gameplay, Adventures has Fox McCloud stepping out of the Arwing and exploring Dinosaur Planet on foot, fighting enemies with a staff and solving environmental puzzles. Adventures also introduced the blue fox character Krystal, who later becomes the first female pilot in Star Fox.
https://twitter.com/NintendoAmerica/status/2097689692883816580
Star Fox Adventures is a particularly divisive entry in the franchise, straying from the flight-combat-simulator roots of the original games and delving into Zelda-like territory. It's also famously Rare's last game for Nintendo before the studio was acquired by Microsoft.
Some fans might argue that Adventures was when the franchise started to go awry, with its follow-ups Assault and Command receiving lukewarm receptions, and the eventual attempted Star Fox Zero is generally looked down on by fans and critics alike. The series did win back goodwill from fans with this year's remake of Star Fox 64 on Switch 2.
Other than the shadowdrop of Star Fox Adventures, the Direct also revealed that a free update is coming to the new Star Fox game, adding new multiplayer features and maps. The Star Fox update launches on September 29.

title: Samus Is Returning To 2D In Metroid Ravenous, And She Talks Again
text:
Today, during the Nintendo Direct livestream , Nintendo announced Metroid Ravenous, a new 2D adventure coming exclusively to Nintendo Switch 2 early next year.
The debut trailer introduced a new group of mysterious villains, as well as a look at some of the new locales Samus will be traveling through to hunt then down. We also see hints of a a new mechanic where Samus "feeds" on enemies to gain extra powers, though exactly how Samus is augmented by feeding is still a mystery.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ku-vSTDNsT8
We also see a new suit, with green armor and a glowing energy sword. This suit was later revealed to be called the Metroid Suit, with an Amiibo figure of the suit included in the Collector's Edition of the game.
Ravenous marks Samus's return to 2D for the first time since 2021's Metroid Dread. Her most recent adventure, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, launched in December after nearly a decade in development.
The Nintendo Direct also featured the reveal of Kirby and the World Beyond, a new open-world adventure starring the famous pink puffball, as well as new editions of Pikmin 4 and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. Third-party announcements during the Direct included Persona 6 coming to Nintendo Switch 2, a Switch 2 edition of Final Fantasy VII Crisis Core Reunion, and a port of Monsters Hunter Wilds.
Metroid Ravenous launches January 28, 2027, exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

title: A New Handheld-Only Switch 2 Game Is Coming From The Silent Hill 2 Remake Devs

The portable-only title will see players becoming "the mysterious Entity," using touch-screen controls to "manipulate reality," according to the YouTube trailer . Bloober Team has talked about this Nintendo project in the past , which was previously referred to as Project M. title: Romancing SaGa 3 Is The Latest Surprise RPG Remake
text:
Square Enix has announced a remake of the 1995 RPG classic, Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United , during the September Nintendo Direct. Billed as a "full 3D remake" by the company, this new version of Romancing SaGa 3 will feature upgraded graphics, fully voiced cutscenes, overhauls to combat and other mechanics, selectable difficulty levels, and several more new features.
Set in a world with scheduled despair, the game follows eight protagonists on their quest to find the survivor of a calamity. Each protagonist has their own reason for doing so, but the driving force behind their actions is the Rise of Morastrum, an event that occurs every 300 years and results in all newborn life being destroyed, save for one survivor, the Child of Destiny.
Like the original game, players will have the opportunity to meet and recruit over 20 other characters along the way, each with individual stats and abilities. These characters can be further fine-tuned with a Nonastrum, a star of fate that the player assigns, which influences their affinity for techs and spells. The Freeform Scenario System will also see player choices shape the characters they meet, and in battle, these warriors can "glimmer" new techniques, gain evasion skills, and perform powerful United Attacks.
Square Enix added that War Mode and the Business minigame will also return, allowing players to command armies or grow a trading empire when they're not busy with the main storyline.
Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United will launch for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch consoles on February 16, 2027. The SaGa series was a hit franchise for Square, with the first entry in the sci-fi RPG kicking off in 1989 on the Game Boy. A pioneer in open-world exploration and non-linear storytelling, Romancing SaGa and other entries in the franchise have periodically cropped up over the years, and in 2024, Square Enix released Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven .

title: GTA 6 Was Not “Fully Formed” When Trailer 1 Came Out In 2023
text:
When Rockstar released GTA 6's first trailer in December 2023, the game looked like it was coming along well, but it wasn't "fully formed" back then. That's according to Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson, who said in an interview that the trailer's song, Tom Petty's "Love is a Long Road" was a "mission statement" for the developers to rally around to get the game finished.
"With the first trailer for this game, the Tom Petty song was a real sort of mission statement. You don’t have the game fully formed, you have an idea of what it’s going to be, but you really have to push hard to pull that together and so when this team is able to do that--and it’s definitely made with everything that you’ve got, but it’s the best of everything you’ve got at that point--it’s put together in such a way that it helps be a bit of a guiding light of what it needs to feel like," he told Trois Couleurs .
Also in the interview, Nelson spoke about how one of the first things the developers did after deciding that GTA 6 would be set in Vice City AKA Miami was to travel there.
"We'll go there. And just  feel  it, and go out and just drive around. Almost always on our own at very first, just a handful of people, and we’ll take a ton of pictures, and soak as much of it up as we can and see what speaks to us and start to talk about it and share ideas about what we want to incorporate," he said.
GTA 6 is set for release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. According to SensorTower's data, the game has already sold 5 million copies via preorders , generating more than $500 million in revenue.
Rockstar is partnered with Sony for GTA 6, and part of that deal includes a GTA 6-themed DualSense controller . It goes on sale September 10 at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET for $85.

title: The Duskbloods Was A No-Show At The September Nintendo Direct And Now I’m Worried
text:
The Duskbloods , From Software's new game and one of the Switch 2's biggest exclusives, was missing-in-action during the September Nintendo Direct .
That normally wouldn't be too shocking, except for the fact The Duskbloods is still slated to release this year. With less than four months to go until the end of the year, the window for The Duskbloods is closing.
One might have assumed the next game from the creators of Elden Ring would receive a release date as part of the presentation, as well as perhaps a glimpse at some of the maps and playable characters not featured in a recent The Duskbloods closed network test. The fact it wasn't shown or mentioned at all is more than a little worrying.
The closed network test for The Duskbloods in August didn't exactly go as planned, with From Software actually cancelling the first day of sessions due to technical difficulties and server issues. Its problems were later resolved for the playtests' subsequent days, allowing players to jump in and take a stab at The Duskbloods' unique blend of cooperative and competitive soulsborne action. It wouldn't be surprising if, given the network test, From Software realized it needed more time to iron out The Duskbloods online multiplayer kinks.
Nintendo could, of course, be waiting to hold a special The Duskbloods Direct in the coming weeks just ahead of the game's launch. It's an approach Nintendo has been fond of more recently, holding dedicated Directs for big games like its Star Fox remake, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and the upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. In the case of Star Fox and Ocarina of Time , both games received release dates as part of their dedicated presentations.
A similar scenario could definitely play out with The Duskbloods, though it's still odd that the game was a no-show at a presentation dedicated to games coming this winter and early next year.
Whether The Duskbloods will release this year, or be pushed into 2027, remains to be seen. Demand, however, is certainly there. A From Software employee recently revealed interest in The Duskbloods playtest surpassed that of Elden Ring Nightreign's .
Though we didn't get another look or release date for The Duskbloods, there were some big announcements during the latest Nintendo Direct. Metroid Ravenous , a new 2D entry in the series, is coming early next year. An open-world Kirby game, Kirby and the World Beyond , is slated for Spring 2027.

title: Shift Up首席技术官回应AI争议
text:
相关文章: Shift Up CEO回应《剑星：血雨》AI宣传片争议
Shift Up首席技术官李东基（DongKi Lee）近日进一步澄清了公司对于AI技术的立场。此前，《剑星：血雨》的一支AI生成音乐视频于上个月引发玩家强烈反弹。
这支音乐视频以一首名为《Wanna be in Love》的轻快流行歌曲作为配乐，使用AI生成的图像和影像，围绕《血雨》主角Evie展开，展示她唱歌、跳舞并穿梭于游戏未来世界中的画面。不过，玩家对此并不买账。视频公开后，不少玩家迅速批评Shift Up没有让公司内部员工参与制作，而是选择使用AI生成内容。
对此，Shift Up CEO金亨泰此前曾公开回应质疑。他表示：「这支视频的核心角色Evie，从头到脚都是由我们优秀的美术师和建模师花费一年多时间亲手打造的。AI并不是从零开始创造她，而是根据我们团队制作的数据、设计和成果，对角色进行呈现和演绎。如果大家能够在理解这一点的基础上看待这部作品，我们会非常感谢。」
如今，随着争议稍微平息，Shift Up首席技术官李东基也进一步解释了这件事。他在9月2日接受TheGamer采访时表示，公司制作这支AI音乐视频，只是希望展示更多Evie所处的世界，而这类内容本质上属于「实验性质」，并不代表正式游戏本身。
李东基表示：「我们公开那支音乐视频，是因为想展示更多《剑星：血雨》的魅力。我们希望进一步展示这个世界，以及角色Evie。我们只是想多展示一点这些内容，所以才把它作为一种内容形式制作出来。」
不过，他也承认，公司非常重视玩家对此表达的不满和担忧。「我们确实认真看待粉丝说的话，以及他们围绕这支音乐视频提出的担忧。从现在开始，我们一定希望把这两类内容明确区分开来，比如一类是与游戏正式内容有关的东西，另一类则是我们所谓的实验性内容，也就是一些正在尝试的东西。」 还有更多相关内容 《剑星》总监谈新主角Evie设计：更年轻但个性更强
李东基随后进一步阐述了Shift Up对于AI技术的整体态度。在他看来，AI应该作为一种「工具」使用，其最终目的应该是帮助团队制作出更好的产品。他说：「AI正在对游戏开发产生很大的影响。但当我们使用某种技术或者工具时，真正重要的是它所服务的方向和目的。它必须以能够支持开发者创造力、经验和技能的方式来使用。它应该是一种工具。这就是我们认为正确的方向，而它最终的目的，应该是帮助我们制作出一款优秀、高质量的游戏。」
不过，这些最新解释显然没有让玩家的态度出现明显好转。不少玩家仍然认为，与其依赖AI来制作宣传音乐视频，Shift Up完全可以让公司内部那些有能力的员工亲自完成。
一名玩家在X上表示：「『展示更多《剑星：血雨》的美』？各位，你们完全可以自己做动画，而且效果肯定好得多。」另一名玩家说道：「他们完全可以自己制作一支音乐视频来『展示更多游戏的美』。笑死。」
近年来，AI在游戏开发中的使用一直是行业内极具争议的话题。多款游戏都曾被卷入类似讨论，其中包括备受期待的《古墓丽影：亚特兰蒂斯遗迹》。开发商Crystal Dynamics已经确认，该作在早期原型阶段使用过AI技术，但同时强调，游戏的「最终成品内容均由人类创作」。
目前仍不清楚《血雨》正式游戏中是否会使用AI技术。不过从李东基最新的表态来看，Shift Up显然将AI视为一种辅助工具，用来帮助开发者发挥创造力与专业技能，并最终提升游戏品质。

相关文章: 世嘉确认取消已公布五年的神秘「超级游戏」项目
世嘉社长兼COO内海州史表示，近年来公司旗下各个IP都出现了越来越多「喜欢作品、但实际上并没有玩过游戏」的粉丝，而在世嘉看来，这些人同样属于玩家。 还有更多相关内容 TGS2025 世嘉/ATLUS展区 公开赠品、舞台节目、商品售卖区等详情
内海州史在9月7日接受Nikkei Gaming采访时，谈到了世嘉目前正在推进的「跨媒体」战略。近年来，包括《刺猬索尼克》《女神异闻录》《如龙》等世嘉旗下重要IP，都开始通过电影、电视剧等形式扩展到游戏之外的不同媒介，以进一步扩大品牌影响力。而这种策略也带来了一个明显变化：越来越多人虽然喜欢这些游戏IP，却从未真正玩过对应的游戏。
Nikkei Gaming主编平野绫在采访中提到：「最近，即便没有玩过游戏，却喜欢某个IP的人似乎越来越多了。」
内海州史回应表示：「近年来，我们每一部作品都出现了越来越多这样的粉丝。比如《如龙》系列的周边商品表现就特别好，其中60%到70%的购买者都是女性。她们可能是通过我们的YouTube频道，或者观看热门YouTuber的直播，喜欢上了《如龙》的世界观、故事和角色。而在这些人当中，有很多其实从来没有真正玩过游戏。」
不过，内海州史并不认为这些人只是「装模作样的假玩家」。相反，无论有没有真正拿起手柄玩过世嘉的游戏，公司都把这些粉丝视为「玩家」。他说：「即使从来没有玩过游戏的人，在我们看来也同样是粉丝，也是玩家。跨媒体战略最大的优势，就是能够增加人们接触IP、对IP产生兴趣的入口和接触点。有些情况下，这些人的参与度甚至比真正玩游戏的粉丝还要高。」
内海州史随后还谈到，女性粉丝在游戏领域的增加，也正在改变发行商设计周边商品的方式。他特别提到了自己过去在Cybird工作的经历。Cybird是一家以女性向恋爱游戏闻名的开发商。内海州史表示：「我在Cybird工作时，也参与过面向女性用户的恋爱游戏。在那里，除了徽章、亚克力立牌这类传统收藏周边之外，我们还看到了周边商品方向上的明显变化。比如服装、化妆品这种日常生活中可以直接使用的授权产品，以及与娱乐设施合作推出的限定和纪念商品，都开始越来越多。那段经历确实拓宽了我的视野，我认为它对于后来制定世嘉的跨媒体战略也非常重要。」
从目前的表现来看，世嘉的「跨媒体」战略已经取得明显成果。三部真人版《刺猬索尼克》电影都在全球票房市场取得了不错成绩，第四部也已经确定制作。与此同时，Netflix目前还在开发《女神异闻录》真人剧集。不过，对于这些影视项目最终能不能把更多观众转化成真正购买游戏的玩家，世嘉似乎并不特别在意。
在世嘉看来，只要喜欢这些IP，无论是否真正玩过游戏，本质上都可以被视为「玩家」。

title: 《塞尔达传说 时之笛》重制版保留读取画面
text:
相关文章: 任天堂公布《塞尔达传说》40周年乐高套装
任天堂确认，《塞尔达传说 时之笛》重制版将有意保留区域切换时的读取画面，目的是「保留原作的精髓」，不过这一决定并没有得到所有玩家认同。
相关信息来自昨晚举行的《塞尔达传说》40周年直面会。在实机演示中，系列制作人青沼英二确认，今年11月登陆Switch 2的《塞尔达传说 时之笛》重制版，会继续保留N64原版中区域之间的读取过程。 还有更多相关内容 《塞尔达传说 时之笛》重制版的40处变化
当林克和娜薇从科奇里森林前往海拉鲁平原时，青沼英二说道：「顺便一提，每当你在不同区域之间移动时，都会出现读取画面。这是我们有意保留下来的，希望借此保留原作的精髓。」
简单回顾一下原版的情况。在1998年的《时之笛》以及此前和此后的许多游戏中，读取画面的作用，就是让开发者暂停游戏过程，并载入接下来供玩家探索的新区域。以原版从科奇里森林进入海拉鲁平原这一段为例，除了前后的一些过场动画之外，玩家实际上只会有几秒钟无法控制林克。
而《时之笛》重制版看起来已经让这个过程变得更加流畅。目前还不清楚青沼英二演示中的表现是否会与最终版本完全一致，不过从画面来看，玩家在控制林克前进后，屏幕会逐渐变黑。随后，右下角会出现一个小型三角力量标志。整个读取过程大约持续3秒，之后幼年林克便会重新出现在画面中。
除去美术风格上的巨大变化之外，任天堂所谓「保留1998年原作精髓」的设计思路，在很多地方确实都与目前展示出的重制方向相符。
不过，《时之笛》发售至今已经接近30年。在这段时间里，游戏行业不断进步，玩家也已经习惯开发者尽可能隐藏读取过程，甚至有不少现代游戏已经基本看不到传统意义上的读取画面。
因此，任天堂选择在《时之笛》重制版中主动保留读取画面，也迅速引发玩家争论。有些玩家很喜欢这种向90年代N64游戏体验致敬的做法。但也有人认为，在现代重制版里主动保留读取画面不仅显得多余，甚至让人有些难以理解。还有部分玩家怀疑，真正的原因其实是Switch 2本身仍然需要读取时间，只是任天堂将其解释成了设计选择。
总之，《塞尔达传说 时之笛》重制版将于2026年11月5日登陆Switch 2。

title: 西谷亮想重做《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》平衡
text:
相关文章: 《街头霸王6》「阿俊」角色预告
《街头霸王2》和《快打旋风》初代设计师之一西谷亮表示，希望重新调整《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》的游戏平衡——距离这款游戏发售已经过去了32年。
2026年9月，也就是《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》于1994年登陆街机厅整整32年后，这位格斗游戏界的传奇人物、资深开发者突然在X上提出了一个颇为大胆的想法：重新给这款老游戏做一次平衡调整。
据EventHubs发现并翻译，西谷亮写道：「《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》还能再调整一下吗？其实当年我并没有参与太多，但如果有机会的话，我还挺想试试的。要是最后变成一场疯狂削弱大会的话，先说声抱歉，哈哈。」
这些年来，卡普空已经多次通过各种复古合集重新推出旗下经典格斗游戏。不过，要说卡普空真的会推出一个彻底重新平衡的原版《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》，似乎还是很难想象。毕竟它至今仍是《街头霸王2》系列中最具代表性的作品之一。
尽管如此，西谷亮本人显然认为，这款游戏值得再调整一次。不过，格斗游戏社区中的部分玩家并不完全认同他的想法。例如，长期从事格斗游戏解说、同时也是格斗游戏社区历史研究者的James Chen就认为，考虑到玩家对原版的喜爱程度，以及这款游戏在社区中的地位，大规模修改很可能不会得到欢迎。
他解释道：「这其实很危险，因为有太多人喜欢现在这个样子的《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》了。说实话，很多看起来逻辑上合理的改动，实际效果可能反而不好。比如取消春丽保留超必杀技蓄力状态的能力，会让这个角色变得没那么有意思；但如果去掉本田可以预先蓄好『大银杏投』的机制，反而会让他变得更有意思——当然，我是说跟他对战的时候。」
另一名玩家也提醒：「《超级街头霸王2X》虽然存在大量不平衡的地方，但它依然是一款非常受欢迎的游戏，而且都已经30多年了，社区现在仍然相当活跃。所以即便真的想重新平衡，也必须非常谨慎地决定到底改什么。」
值得注意的是，西谷亮目前已经不在卡普空任职。他在1995年创办了自己的游戏开发公司ARIKA，并一直工作至今。格斗游戏玩家对这家工作室最熟悉的作品，可能是《Fighting EX Layer》。这款游戏也被视为上世纪90年代《街头霸王EX》系列的精神续作。 还有更多相关内容 《街头霸王6》「亚思敏」更新上线宣传视频
事实上，这些年来卡普空也曾多次推出《超级街头霸王2 Turbo》的不同版本。2008年，公司推出了《超级街头霸王2 Turbo HD Remix》，当时获得了媒体普遍好评。2017年，卡普空又在Switch上推出《终极街头霸王2》，同样是在原作基础上重新制作，加入了更新后的画面、新角色以及平衡性调整。不过，如今《街头霸王6》正处于成功运营阶段，卡普空是否还有兴趣再次大规模翻修这些经典旧作，目前仍然很难判断。

title: PlayStation架构师Mark Cerny成立基金扶持新人
text:
相关文章: 神谷英树：游戏保存比实体数字之争更重要
PlayStation架构师Mark Cerny表示，自己的职业生涯已经「接近尾声」，希望在真正离开行业之前，把自己得到过的帮助继续传递给下一代游戏开发者。
为此，他与TGA创始人Geoff Keighley合作成立了名为「The Nova Games Foundation」的全新非营利基金会，计划每年为20名游戏设计相关专业毕业生提供六位数美元规模的资助。 还有更多相关内容 索尼拒绝向玩家返还关税退款
Geoff Keighley（左）与Mark Cerny（右）
Cerny与Keighley在接受Game File采访时正式公布了这一项目。两人表示，Nova Games Foundation的目标不是只运作几年，而是希望持续数十年。除了提供导师指导外，入选者还将获得10万美元的「无附加条件」资助。如果部分项目开发进展特别顺利，申请者还可以获得额外最高50万美元的资金支持，具体是否追加资助，将根据项目能否完成相应开发里程碑决定。
Cerny对Game File记者Stephen Totilo表示：「我的职业生涯已经接近尾声了。我还没有结束，但这些日子里，我经常在想，怎样才能用最好的方式，把自己得到过的帮助继续传递下去。」
Keighley则表示：「我一直都想回馈这个行业，但考虑到自己在行业中的身份，我从来不觉得自己适合以商业方式投资游戏。我从来没有持有过游戏公司的股票，也没有在某款游戏中拥有财务利益。Nova是一项公益项目：我们不会拿股权，也不打算收回这些资助。我们希望得到的回报是创作层面的——帮助新的声音做出游戏，并在行业里站稳脚跟。」
Hazelight创始人兼游戏总监Josef Fares已经确认会通过捐款和导师指导的方式参与其中。Fares此前负责过《逃出生天》《双人成行》和《双影奇境》等双人合作游戏。
与此同时，纽约大学和南加州大学也将成为首批参与项目的学校之一。目前共有来自世界各地的13所大学加入Nova Games Foundation计划。
第一批资助对象将来自这些学校的2026届和2027届毕业生，申请将于今年12月正式开放。
