title: 生存专家约翰·哈德森盛赞《沙丘：觉醒》沙漠「真到难以置信」
text:
相关文章: 《沙丘：觉醒》宣传视频
在《沙丘：觉醒》9月22日主机版发售前夕，英国军方生存顾问约翰·哈德森在一段全新视频中，带你审视厄拉科斯背后致命的生存现实。
要真正在厄拉科斯上生存下来，究竟需要什么？在一段全新特辑中，英国军方首席生存教官兼顾问约翰·哈德森审视了《沙丘：觉醒》沙漠世界背后致命的生存现实，从补水、庇护所，到沙暴来袭时的暴露风险、资源管理，乃至群体协作求生，逐一解析。
凭借在沙漠等极端环境中设计与开展生存训练的丰富经验，哈德森着重强调了《沙丘：觉醒》中那些经风沙雕琢的岩层与严酷地貌的高度写实感。
「《沙丘：觉醒》团队打造的那些岩石露头逼真得令人难以置信，」哈德森表示，「它们看上去就像历经沙漠风暴的沙蚀打磨，如同被风雕刻而成。然而在它们之中，你又能看到一丝可以栖身避难的希望。」
哈德森进一步探讨了游戏严酷的环境如何映照现实世界的沙漠生存法则：抵御极端高温与烈日暴晒、节约用水、在沙暴来袭时寻找庇护，并依靠团队协作携带生存所需的资源。
该特辑还剖析了厄拉科斯为何不只是一个故事背景，它更像是一场主动出击的生存挑战：玩家必须为每一次出行做足准备、搭建庇护所、管理稀缺资源、结盟求生，并与这颗星球上体型巨大的沙虫周旋。 还有更多相关内容 PS5版《沙丘：觉醒》实机演示 | gamescom 2026
《沙丘：觉醒》是 Funcom 打造的一款开放世界生存游戏，灵感源自弗兰克·赫伯特（Frank Herbert）的开创性科幻小说与传奇影业（Legendary Entertainment）屡获殊荣的电影作品。游戏将于2026年9月22日登陆主机平台，豪华版与终极版玩家可自9月17日起抢先开玩。主机玩家，以及新加入和回归的 PC 玩家，都将体验到自 PC 版发售以来引入的所有新增内容与改进，以及将于9月上线的新内容与更新。

title: Switch 2版《最终幻想7 核心危机 再融合》宣传视频 | 任天堂直面会
text:
游戏现已发售
《最终幻想7 核心危机》自2007年发售以来，因为其感人的故事而深受众多玩家喜爱。本作除了将画面HD化之外，包括登场角色在内的所有3D模型也将焕然一新。支持全语音的内容和全新改编的乐曲将更加生动地描绘出连结《最终幻想7》的故事。玩家能够在其中享受到更美丽的画面、更易玩的系统，体验超越HD复刻的进化。游戏现已登录Switch 2平台。

title: NOVA海外独立游戏见闻 Vol.151
text:
Vol.151（9 月第 1 周）
本期见闻覆盖时间：8 月 31 日至 9 月 6 日
本期整理： dxmi
行业见闻录
Nexus Mods 收购数据库网站 SteamDB
9 月 2 日，模组网站 Nexus Mods 与数据库网站 SteamDB 分别于官网宣布，SteamDB 已被 Nexus Mods 全资收购。收购之后，SteamDB 将会获得来自 Nexus Mods 的资金与团队支持，仍维持独立并保留原有品牌。
SteamDB 创始人 xPaw 在声明中称，他最初是出于兴趣和热情创建了 SteamDB，但网站的发展已经远远超出了他最初的预期。随着另一位创始人 Marlamin 在数年前退出项目，xPaw 运营网站投入的时间已经相当于一份全职工作，不断增长的工作量令他感到难以为继。今年年初，xPaw 试图寻找一位靠谱的合作伙伴以继续网站的运营，而 Nexus Mods 在此时联系了他。
Nexus Mods 在声明中表示，模组常常需要基于特定游戏版本运行，而 SteamDB 记录了大量与游戏版本和更新相关的历史数据，将这些数据与模组管理工具结合将会使模组的运行更为可靠。而对于 SteamDB 的用户而言，SteamDB 仍然会维持一直以来的使用体验，用户也不会被强迫关联 Nexus Mods 账号。
Nexus Mods x SteamDB/图片： SteamDB
Aggro Crab 推出新独立游戏发行品牌
9 月 2 日，曾推出《蟹蟹寻宝奇遇》并参与发行《Peak》的独立游戏工作室兼发行商 Aggro Crab 通过 官网 宣布将推出一个新发行品牌，旨在支持“风格强烈、个性鲜明、充满态度的游戏”。该发行品牌将由 Aggro Crab 直接运营，主要面向小型开发团队，为那些预计能在两年或更短时间内完成的项目提供最高 50 万美元的资金支持。
在该品牌达成的发行合作中，Aggro Crab 将提供较为灵活的合作协议，包括统一的基础条款，可调整的阶段性目标，并且不强制要求项目 100%收回成本，也不会将最后一笔款项扣留至游戏发售时才支付。此外，该发行品牌还将协助开发团队进行市场推广，包括制作预告片、主视觉图、提供品牌发展建议，以及通过 Aggro Crab 的社交媒体渠道宣传其作品等。目前，Aggro Crab 已经签下两个项目：ThirtyThree 开发的平台跳跃游戏《Rebounder》，以及 Bubby Darkstar 开发的恐怖游戏《Subway Midnight》。
Aggro Crab 官方表示：“这些年来，我们的声誉和影响力在不断扩大，因此我们希望尝试帮助独立开发者打开一些他们通常难以接触的门路。不过，我们并不打算干涉别人，或在开发者不希望的情况下强加任何创意控制。如果我们决定与你合作，那是因为我们认为你拥有一个非常酷的愿景，并且我们相信你能够完全按照自己的想法将它实现。”
图片： Aggro Crab
科隆展主办方就独立开发者设备被盗事件道歉
此前在 8 月 28 日，一位独立开发者在 社交媒体 发文，称其存放在科隆展商务馆独立展位的笔记本电脑遭到盗窃，很快又有 其他开发者 报告了类似的遭遇。设备失窃导致前者大幅压缩展会行程，且几位开发者的新作开发数据面临暴露风险。8 月 29 日，科隆展主办方通过 社交媒体 做出回应，但“建议参展商为设备投保”的冷淡态度在社交平台引发了大范围不满。
9 月 4 日，科隆展主办方 再次发布文章 ，对此前回应开发者设备被盗事件时所展现的沟通态度正式道歉。主办方称已经开始与几位开发者联系，以了解盗窃事件对其造成的影响并获取他们的诉求。主办方还对在事件发生后迅速对开发者展开援助的公司及个人表示感激，也承认这并不能免除主办方在安保方面的责任。接下来，主办方将认真调研来自参展者的反馈，并召开会议讨论，以制定具体的安保改进方案。
文章末尾，主办方表示：“科隆展因游戏行业而生，也是为了游戏行业而生。它依靠无数人的热情不断发展，而这其中也包括众多对我们而言至关重要的小型工作室。一直以来，我们的承诺都是让 gamescom 变得更好——我们不能只在一切顺利时，才与社区站在一起。这正是此时此刻我们所要做的。感谢每一位正在帮助我们的人。”
主办方的道歉声明/图片： Twi/X
Ukie 推出独立开发者市场培训项目
9 月 1 日，Ukie（英国娱乐休闲软件发行商协会）通过 官网 宣布，其与社群服务平台 Discord 和市场营销咨询公司 Gameflex 共同推出“市场推广学院”（Go To Market Academy）这一旨在支持英国独立游戏工作室的商业培训项目。注册地址位于英国的游戏工作室可于 9 月 30 日前申请参与。
该项目由六个线上模块组成，内容覆盖市场诊断与洞察、营销战略与宣传活动执行、运用 Discord 进行社区互动，以及工作室品牌建设等主题。据悉，项目将面向 10 至 12 家工作室开放，并于下个月在伦敦举行的 EGX 与 MCM Comic Con 活动期间，以一场线下课程正式启动，线上课程将持续至 11 月及 12 月初。
UKIE 首席执行官 Nick Poole 表示：“许多有潜力的游戏最终在市场推广阶段遭遇挫折，并不是因为工作室缺乏好的创意，而是因为他们没有足够的时间和支持，去建立能够让这些创意真正成长起来的社区。‘市场推广学院’为独立工作室提供了一个认真解决这些问题的空间，参与者同时还能获得 Discord 官方的直接支持。”
Go To Market Academy/图片： Ukie
索尼 9 月 State of Play 发布会引玩家不满
9 月 3 日，索尼播出了 2026 年 9 月 State of Play 线上发布会，并紧随其后播出了 State of Play 日本发布会。尽管两场发布会带来了超过 30 款游戏的最新信息，但由于缺乏新作以及索尼近期取消实体盘的计划，大量玩家在其 社交媒体 评论区表达了对此次发布会的不满。
此外，根据第三方数据平台 Streams Charts 统计，本场 State of Play 的观众峰值与观众观看时长均明显下滑，仅为 6 月 State of Play 发布会的三分之一左右。与 2 月的 State of Play 发布会相比，本次的观众峰值与观看时长也仅为其一半左右。
图片： State of Play
Xbox 限制 XGP 会员云游戏时长
9 月 3 日，Xbox 通过 官方博客 宣布，将于 11 月起限制 XGP 用户的免费云游戏时长，Ultimate、Premium 和 Essential 会员每月可分别获得 15 小时、10 小时与 5 小时的免费云游戏时间。在此之前，符合条件的用户仍可进行不限时的免费云游戏体验。
自 11 月起，在免费云游戏时间耗尽后，XGP 用户需要在 Xbox 商店另行购买云游戏时长。届时云游戏也将与 XGP 解绑，玩家即使不订阅 XGP，也可以直接从 Xbox 商店购买云游戏时长，并在受支持的设备上运行云游戏。玩家甚至可以在 Xbox One 上通过云游戏体验 Xbox Series X|S 的游戏内容。
Xbox 官方在博客文章中称：“我们之所以推出这一模式，是因为随着使用云游戏的人越来越多，游戏时间越来越长，提供云游戏服务的成本也随之上升。改为按月设定使用额度，可以让我们继续提供这项服务，同时持续投入资源提升其稳定性和性能。”
图片： Xbox
观点：业界正在经历雅达利大崩溃后的第二次大崩溃？
9 月 3 日， 媒体 GamesIndustry 报道 ，《Edge》杂志采访了九位业内专家，请他们谈谈所谓的“崩溃 2.0”，以及他们认为游戏行业未来可能走向何方。EPIC 首席执行官 Tim Sweeney 在采访中称，游戏行业正在经历自 20 世纪 80 年代以来最严重的一次崩溃。
Sweeney 提出，行业一方面面临产业内部的结构性失调，例如 3A 游戏开发成本过高，一些游戏的开发预算已经达到 2.5 亿至 4 亿美元。而另一方面，游戏业也受到外部挑战，尤其是近期的硬件短缺：“如今，全球正掀起一轮前所未有的 AI 系统和数据中心投资热潮，其背后的信念是这些技术将对经济产生真正的变革性影响。而巨大的经济机会意味着，这些领域可以在所有零部件的争夺中压过整个娱乐产业。”
Playable Worlds 首席执行官 Raph Koster 认为，走出“崩溃 2.0”的唯一办法就是使整个行业重置，但 AI 并非解决之道。“我们的行业具有周期性。除非我们迎来某种技术奇点，否则总会有某个平台（译注：例如雅达利崩溃后的任天堂）出现，改变整个局面。AI 并不是一种能够让成本下降的平台级重置。AI 只是让计算机变得更强大，因此资源消耗还会不断增加……归根结底，它实际上极其昂贵，所以大部分收益都会向上游流动。AI 确实正在非常迅速地改变很多事情，但这（对于行业所面临的结构性问题而言）也无关紧要。”
雅达利大崩溃/图片： Wikipedia
独游公告板
一周拾遗 ：本周值得关注的新发售、重新上架或公布新版本的独立游戏。
1. 9 月 2 日，由 Lefto Studio 制作的欢乐向合作游戏《BOMBANANA!》正式发售，并于 3 天内累计获得超过 700 条好评，达到“好评如潮”。
《BOMBANANA!》是一款让人鸡飞狗跳的合作拆弹游戏，三名玩家分别扮演不见猴、不听猴和不言猴，各自掌握部分情报，必须默契配合拆除炸弹，稍有不慎就会集体升天！你们的友谊能否经受住这样的终极考验呢？
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4656000/BOMBANANA/
2. 9 月 4 日，由 CanOpener 制作的黑暗奇幻风格策略游戏《地城拓荒 Dungeon Settlers》发布了 EA 测试版，仅仅两天就斩获 400 条评价并达到“特别好评”。
作为由公会派遣的探险队队长，你的任务是探索、征服并摧毁那个带来一切灾厄的地下城。为此，你需要在荒芜之地上建立据点，战略性地培养队员，并为即将到来的危险做好准备。在可实时暂停的战术战斗中，没有回合或回合数限制，你必须分析敌人的特性与行动模式，以战术压制对手赢得胜利。但请记住：死亡，是永恒的别离……
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2798330/_Dungeon_Settlers/
开发追踪： 本周更新开发关键节点、尚处在开发早期或中期的独立游戏。
1. 9 月 2 日，《活体脑细胞》制作组 Frictional Games 新作《ONTOS》公布了一段长达 10 分钟的实机演示，维持了制作组一贯的科幻悬疑风格。
“一段科幻悬疑故事，在改造后的月球旅馆‘森索洛’拉开序幕。神秘实验与诡异遭遇交织成难解的谜团，等你来一一探明。随着探索的深入，真相逐步浮出水面，你将面对那个终极问题：现实究竟是什么？”
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2924520/ONTOS/
2. 9 月 2 日，由 ThirtyThree 开发的漫画风格平台动作游戏《Rebounder》发布首个预告，展现了其独特的美术风格。
“精准完成每一次冲刺，漂亮地抵达终点。《Rebounder》是一款纯手工打造的平台跳跃游戏，讲述了一名粗犷的工人被招募前往遥远星球，执行一项危险任务的故事。游戏是一场艰难而公平的挑战，舞台则是一个由墨水、纸张与印刷品构成的超现实漫画世界。”
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3794520/Rebounder/
3. 9 月 5 日，由 Raw Power Games 开发的《Chronicles: Medieval》发布新预告，着重介绍了游戏中的大地图系统。
“踏入波澜壮阔、瞬息万变的中世纪沙盒世界，体验百年战争时代的刀光剑影。探索这个残酷壮美、基于真实历史构建的欧洲大陆；率领军队投身宏大战役；在一场场战斗中逐步扬名立万，留下足以载入史册的光辉事迹。你将书写怎样的传奇？”
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2231020/Chronicles_Medieval/
Demo 体验： 本周上线 Demo、或可一试的独立游戏一览。
1. 《开拓物语》
关键字：休闲、冒险、角色扮演、农场模拟；《开拓物语》是一款融合了战术撤离与领地建设的冒险种田游戏。锻造独特武器，去探索世界，寻找稀有宝物，在这个治愈赛璐璐动画风格打造的奇幻世界里，与个性十足的伙伴们一同开拓继承自先祖的遗落领地。收集资源，建造村庄，链接羁绊，勤劳致富，亲手创造超酷的顶级家园！
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4829780/_/

关键字：自走棋、轻度 Rogue、增量；《Idle Pixel Battle》是一款奇幻题材的放置自动战斗游戏，核心玩法围绕战利品、升级和持续成长展开。组建英雄队伍，观看他们自动对抗一波又一波的怪物。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4809070/Idle_Pixel_Battle/

关键字：休闲、增量、物理；发射弹珠！强化盘面！赚取堆成山的奖牌，不断还清一笔又一笔债务！一款流程紧凑的柏青哥增量游戏，技能树会不断带来新的赚钱方式！
https://store.steampowered.com/app/5062970/Incremental_Pachinko_Heaven/
4. 《ShredDead》
关键字：增量、自走棋、策略；《ShredDead》是一款轻松搞怪的渐进式僵尸绞杀放置游戏，核心在于不断成长，而且没有失败条件。击败无尽尸潮、收集战利品、壮大技能树，并让僵尸不断进化。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4704520/ShredDead/

关键字：动作类 Rogue、角色扮演；《零境·入侵》是一款 3D 横版动作肉鸽游戏。化身时间骇客，游走在不同时间线中，充分利用动作技巧与战斗策略，收集关键道具，找到关键线索，拼凑出真相，打败虚世之主——耶罗索！真相，真的仅仅是这样吗？
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4061170/_/

关键字：心理恐怖、探索、解谜；这款游戏的开发者在完成作品之前失踪了。探索他最后一个项目的重构版本：一款第一人称心理恐怖游戏，每个章节都隐藏着新的规则，而这座房子似乎记得曾经来过这里的人。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4712780/Project_Spooky/
7. 《Trolley Dilemma》
关键字：冒险、多结局、喜剧、哲理；直面无解的两难抉择，结识形形色色的怪诞角色，见证每一次道岔切换如何改写故事。电车不断前行，而你的选择将决定你信任谁、背叛谁，以及最终是否会变成自己从未想成为的那种人。

我是一名知名外企 CEO（非游戏行业）。
我想做解压类小游戏。不是因为它好赚，是因为我研究了几年"人在什么状态下会觉得舒服"这件事，而游戏是我见过把这件事做得最直接的媒介——你按一下，世界真的变了；你做完一件事，你真的知道自己做完了。这两件事在现实生活里越来越难得。

但我也知道，共创不是所有人都想要的。
有人就是想安安稳稳做活拿钱，不想操心方向、不想背项目死活的风险、也不想等一个不确定的分成。这个想法完全正当，我不觉得它比共创低一等。

title: Final Fantasy 14: Dawntrail's final story patch is exactly what the game needed, and has the 4-month wait for Evercold suddenly feeling a whole lot longer
text:
The reception to Final Fantasy 14: Dawntrail's story has been as much of a journey as the expansion itself. It was never going to be easy, being the first expansion to build a brand-new arc following a decade of excellent storytelling, and unfortunately it didn't quite land initially.
Criticisms around its core narrative have largely abated over the last few patches, though, as we near the next expansion Evercold in January. And with its final batch of quests now unleashed upon players I'm here to declare: this might be the greatest final MSQ patch we've ever received.
Spoilers ahead for Patch 7.56 of Dawntrail, if that wasn't already obvious.
Dawntrail's final quests serve as less of a light teaser for what's to come in Evercold, and instead feel like a straight-up prologue to the expansion. That's wildly different from what I've come to expect from these patch quests. Sure, we usually spend a few patches building up to what's next, dropping little hints and then using the final patch quests to introduce a new character or setting as a fun little hype-builder.
But this felt… different, somehow. Almost as if we were playing the first few quests of Evercold. The patch already goes ahead and drops us straight into the ice-clad Fourth—that's the reflection we'll be spending our time in during the expansion—and almost immediately into an encounter against foes we'll undoubtedly face in the future.
(Image credit: Square Enix) Our character introduction teaser comes in the form of Visna, an adorable young catgirl with her wits about her and a dab hand with a crossbow. Oh yeah, that's the other thing: this patch seems to be straight-up showing off the currently unrevealed physical ranged job. Creative Studio 3 still seems to be keeping its cards somewhat close to its chest with it, though. Visna doesn't have many animations, aside from one move where she cleaves clusters of enemies and calls out to her falcon.
But just being able to see it, without even knowing anything about it, is the exact sort of pre-expansion hype I'm a total sucker for. Coupled with Visna charismatically explaining what the Fourth's all about: Differently-branded folks confined to certain homes, all of which happen to be gigantic airships on account of the surface being completely frozen over for the last 500 years. Get too close to someone with a different brand? Well, according to Visna, there's a good chance one or both of you will die for it. It's a great opportunity to info dump in advance, already letting us know what we're in for.
The whole thing builds up to getting us ready to head to Evercold's first location, Naglfar, while cleverly confining us to a tiny, separate area that still gives us a glimpse of what sort of vibe we can anticipate. The real thing'll come with Evercold itself, naturally, but it felt like I was already able to dip a toe into the expansion even while restricted to a singular floating platform.
(Image credit: Square Enix) Everything ends right before we plan to set off to Naglfar, leaving Evercold in the perfect position to throw us straight into the action. Not that I mind a little new-expansion-preamble, but Creative Studio 3 slapping it in the previous expansion is a great way to get the ball rolling on the next one even quicker than it might usually be able to. It was all incredibly refreshing in a way I simply had not expected, and I could feel myself getting those new-expansion fuzzy feelings even with Evercold four entire months away.
I think it's an excellent direction for Dawntrail's final moments to take—especially in an expansion that has been largely disparaged on the narrative front—setting the stage in a way that feels a little bit different to expansions past. It's still difficult to tell what sort of expansion Evercold is going to be based on a relatively short batch of quests, but I'm incredibly excited to find out.

title: Over 1,000 cut voice lines from Resident Evil 4 and Requiem reveal more about Leon Kennedy, the zombies he fights, and a lowkey bromance
text:
Resident Evil is one of those series which rewards nosey players. There's always notes, recordings, and pictures hidden in the cracks and crevices, all of which give players more info. Whether that be the structural integrity, of Mr. X's trench coat or the fact that Grace Ashcroft has absolutely zero social life.
But it's not just all about notes—there's also a great deal of information given in Resident Evil games via their seemingly throwaway voice lines. So, with that in mind, one leaker has just found the motherlode.
(Image credit: Capcom) Notable community modder Keff0 has posted two videos to YouTube over the last week. One goes through over 600 cut voice lines from the Resident Evil 4 remake , and the other explores nearly 400 cut voice lines from Resident Evil Requiem .
The Resident Evil 4 remake deep dive into the scrapped voice lines is certainly interesting, as we hear more from Leon, Ashley, Luis, and the Merchant. Hearing more from Leon is always a win, but the prize for 'most notable cut voice' line has to go to the Merchant, as he sneaks in a reference to Resident Evil Village .
"Ah, I see you're no stranger to villages," the Merchant says in a cut line from the RE4 remake. "The Duke? Lad shows promise." This is likely referring to The Duke from Resident Evil Village, who acts as the resident merchant and something of a guide to Ethan Winters.
(Image credit: Capcom) Funny thing is, The Duke has also mentioned RE4's Merchant before, saying "What're ya buyin?" to Ethan before joking that it was "just something an old friend of mine used to say."
Both characters are also similar in that they seem omnipresent, omniscient, and unkillable, popping up at random across the map unscathed and knowing far more about what's going on than they perhaps should. Although the Merchant may not be as immortal as he once seemed, as Keff0 also uncovered unused animations for their death scene, suggesting that at one point during development players were able to kill him.
(Image credit: Capcom) The cut voice lines for Requiem may not hold any connections to different Resident Evil games, but they do have masses of information about its characters and, crucially, the infected.
We already knew that the strain of the T-virus in Requiem was slightly different , in that it allowed infected to retain some memories of their past life and repeat some familiar actions like scrubbing the floors, eating, or singing. If you listened closely as well you could also hear the infected crying and asking for forgiveness.
But thanks to the cut voice lines found by Keff0, we now know that it could've been so much worse. Burning zombies would beg for water while screaming about how much the flames hurt. The huge Chunk would plead that he didn't want to die and cry about how stressed he was. Some infected would even thank you once you put them out of their misery.
(Image credit: Capcom) The lines we did get were certainly enough to hammer home just how tragic it all was. But I can't help but feel a little sad that we missed out on some of these. I think I would've actually felt sorry for Chunk had I heard him whining about how stressed he was—it's certainly relatable.
Then there's Leon's cut lines. Most of them are just his usual grunts and groans along with some spider-themed quips—there's so many spider quips. But the most interesting line comes towards the end of the game, when he's really starting to suffer the effects of his infection and multiple monstrous fights: "I promise I'll make it home."
It may not seem like a lot. But given how sombre Leon's been ever since Resident Evil 2, it's actually quite significant that Leon came back to Raccoon City not as some hail mary mission to save Sherry and redeem his previous shortcomings, but with the intention of moving on and living his life away from its shadow.
Sadly, we were never going to be able to have all of these lines in Requiem or the Resident Evil 4 remake—there simply isn't the space to fit them all in. But at least we got to see what could have been.

title: Just days after The Tetris Company warned that 'we take copyright infringement very seriously,' the Tetris clone in the White House Arcade suddenly disappears
text:
Last week, The White House, the seat of power in a country that really has better things to be doing, rolled out a virtual arcade containing five very bad videogames, including one based on the famed block-stacking game Tetris. Unlike what we've seen in past instances where videogame properties were used without permission in White House propaganda, The Tetris Company quickly called it out, warning, "We take copyright infringement very seriously."
And now, that game—called Build the Wall—is gone.
Most of the games in the White House Arcade promote various elements of US president Donald Trump's agenda: Rio Run promotes racism and xenophobia, Supply Line focuses on the virtues of science denial, and Trump Savings Tycoon extols the upsides of corruption. Build the Wall was all about stoking fears of immigration: Stacked blocks represented a wall keeping people—very specifically Mexicans, described by the game as "the coming horde"—from entering the US.
It was a very bad game that didn't seem to work entirely correctly, but nonetheless it was undeniably a Tetris clone, and it prompted a response from The Tetris Company on Instagram : "At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them. To our fans everywhere: We love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community." The Tetris Company also clarified that it was not involved in the making of the game, and issued that indirect but hard-to-miss warning about copyright.
When exactly the game was removed isn't known, but its absence was first noticed today by This Week in Video Games ; the Internet Archives' Wayback Machine indicates the game was still present on the site as of around 9 pm ET on September 7.
What makes Build the Wall's removal so interesting is how The Tetris Company's response stands in such contrast to the silence of other companies whose properties have been used in the White House's prolific social media posting. Halo, Destiny 2, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, and Pokémon have all featured prominently in such posts; more recently, the White House has used Xbox, Nintendo, and Sega logos to promote its new arcade.
CAN'T STOP WINNING. 🎮Build the wall. Deport. Fill a Trump Account. LIVE - PLAY NOW 📲 https://t.co/qIR69AxSnm pic.twitter.com/2nr2jG1ZRg September 3, 2026
The Pokémon Company said it hadn't granted permission for the use of its characters in the posts, and Japan's Foreign Ministry has reportedly asked the US government, behind closed doors, to please stop . But as far as I know this is the first time anyone has explicitly called out the White House's unauthorized use of intellectual properties in public, and implied the possibility of action over it.
Of course there's no confirmed connection between The Tetris Company's insinuation of trouble and the sudden takedown of the Tetris clone from the White House Arcade, and it could just be a coincidence that the one company to push back on this sort of garbage is the one company to get action on it. But it could be that there's a lesson to be learned here, too. I've reached out to The Tetris Company and the White House to ask if it's a coincidence or something more, and will update if I receive a reply.

title: Breaking Benjamin frontman pauses concert to rant about Fallout 4 modding beef: 'There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me'
text:
Local Man Benjamin Burnley interrupts a Breaking Benjamin concert with a rant about his True First Person 1.2 Fallout 4 mod  from  r/Fallout An amazing scene played out over the weekend at a Breaking Benjamin concert in Holmdel, NJ, as captured by Reddit user im_all_ears (embedded above).
Band frontman Benjamin Burnley spent over four minutes imploring the audience to download his Fallout 4 mod in an effort to stick it to another modder who Burnley says bullied him over the quality of his work.
"There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me and bullying me, saying, 'Oh, your mod is shit. You don't know what you're fucking doing,'" said Burnley. "So I'm doing this every fucking night, and blowing his fucking downloads out of the water."
That was a mere two minutes into the four-and-a-half minute rant. Someone behind the scenes at the venue even joined in, putting the mod's details up on screens.
"Even if you fuckin' don't play that game, go and download it. It's on Nexus Mods," said Burnley. "Tomorrow I better see all my motherfuckin' downloads going up."
One attendee shouted: "Play some music!" Others in the crowd were loving it. Burnley kept going, telling the audience to wait for his new update to drop before downloading the mod.
"When you post a mod, you're supposed to be able to grow and learn and make it better," Burnley said. "And right off the bat, this fucking asshole was shitting on my mod."
Sure enough, the mod, which is called 'True First Person,' was last updated on Sunday. Here's how Burnely describes the mod on its Nexus Mods page :
"Fallout 4's vanilla first person shows a pair of floating arms. This mod replaces that with a True First Person perspective where your player character's full body is rendered and visible in first person. Look down and you'll see your body, legs, clothing and equipped gear as part of the same character you see in third person. Your perspective also stays in first person during interactions that would normally force the camera out, such as workstations, power armor, etc."
The mod is tagged "AI assisted," so presumably an amount of vibe coding went into it. The comments are now full of fans reacting to the concert, so actual assessments of how well it works are hard to come by, but Burnley has posted a video of the mod in action .
"Brother I'm at your concert right now. You have my download," reads one post on the mod's page. Burnley, whose Nexus Mods username is "killemloud," thanked the poster that same night, after the show.
Breaking Benjamin was formed in 1999, and has a previous connection to gaming: the single "Blow Me Away," which it recorded for the Halo 2 soundtrack.

title: Inspired by the success of games like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, French president Emmanuel Macron declares 'videogames are part of our culture' and announces a new international gaming festival
text:
One of the biggest videogames of 2025 was Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , a French JRPG that sold millions of copies, won armloads of awards, and earned not just one but two separate shout-outs from French President Emmanuel Macron. It must've made an even bigger impression on him than it first appeared, as over the weekend Macron announced a new "international videogame festival" that will take place in France.
Macron made the announcement during an address at the Lumiere Summit (via GamesRadar ), a conference where governments, businesses, creators, and "cultural institutions" can collaborate on the future of "cinema and the moving image." I assume that last bit is a just-missed translation of "motion picture," because that's clearly what the conference is about, but regardless, Macron used the moment to reveal his ambitions for a related-but-different effort.
"I firmly believe that videogames are part of our culture," Macron said (Google translated), adding that games should be considered part of France's cultural heritage, just as movies and "other creative endeavors" already are.
"Therefore, we will create an international videogame festival conceived from the outset as a major global event for creativity, innovation, gamers, and the industry. The great global successes of French videogames remind us of the richness of this creative endeavor, this creativity, which is also an industry. We must further celebrate it and strive to gain everyone's support."
Parce que les jeux vidéo font partie de notre culture, nous allons créer un festival international du jeu vidéo. pic.twitter.com/45g7UYfOzk September 7, 2026
Macron didn't mention Clair Obscur by name, but that has to be at the top of his mind. There's really no bigger outwardly French videogame of the moment, and as I said, he's called it out publicly at least twice in the past.
But there are an awful lot of other really good made-in-France videogames out there. Ubisoft, headquartered in Saint-Mandé, France, makes quite a few of them, and there's also the Plague Tale series, Rematch , Jusant , Chants of Sennaar , Sifu , Stray , and casting a little further back, the biggest and best of them all (and this is not up for discussion), Another World.
Details of Macron's proposed new showcase weren't shared, but he did offer some insight into what he called " profound upheavals " in film, television, animation, and videogames, including artificial intelligence and the advent of platforms—I imagine a reference to things like Roblox, Netflix, and Paramount if it ever manages to complete the Warner acquisition—that "are transforming our habits."
"Faced with challenges that know no borders, no nation can act alone. That is why, in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, France and South Korea—two great nations of creation committed to cultural diversity and their sovereignty—are bringing together those who create, produce, finance, distribute, innovate, and decide. Our ambition: to forge new alliances between creators and technologies, public and private actors, cinema, television, platforms, and video games. So that this revolution opens up new possibilities without homogenizing our imaginations."
(Image credit: Emmanuel Macron (Twitter)) France already has one big videogame festival, Paris Games Week, but it's possible Macron is envisioning something more in the way of a cultural exchange program rather than a business-oriented event. We'll have to wait and see for that, just as we're now waiting to see what Clair Obscur developer Sandfall Interactive gets up to next .

title: Thousand Hells is a 'tactical narrative' feast of infernal storytelling, but its defeats can feel brutal
text:
In Thousand Hells: The Underworld heists, I've sort of taken on the role of the dad in that one tweet about feeding cats to coyotes. But rather than serving up pets to jackals, I'm dutifully feeding bands of doomed adventurers into the psychological, corporeal, and spiritual wood chipper of the "tactical narrative" game's bespoke hellscapes.
Those hellscapes—from the primordial twilight taigas of the Midnight North, to the melting fever-dream dominion of the Hell of Nightmares—form a mesmerizing kaleidoscope of abyssal imagination. Made by the developer behind the phenomenal King of Dragon Pass and Six Ages games , its pedigree is obvious as each game guides my hand-picked party of hell raiders through encounters rich with the implied culture, tradition, and history of their respective afterlives.
I just wish I weren't spending quite as much time feeling like my efforts are futile.
(Image credit: Kitfox Games) A game of Thousand Hells, designed for quicker, more repeatable sessions than developer A Sharp's prior work, begins in the Eternal City, a metropolis where the thousand worlds conjoin, and from which daring (or foolish) heroes can embark for their thousand associated underworlds. After a quick character creation process, I'm given a task by a benefactor—reclaiming the spirits of two murdered princes, for example—that I'll need to embark into one of four hells to complete.
If I hope to have any chance of survival, however, I'll need a party, gathered through a team-building process in which I'm cobbling together an incomplete picture of my potential recruits' talents and traits. Those traits will serve as Thousand Hells' basic gameplay mechanic: As my party and I embark for more demonic climes, I'll be playing our traits as game tiles during the randomized set of turn-based trials we'll encounter.
The better those traits match the task at hand, the better my dice roll will be for surpassing a challenge. If my party finds itself being forced to navigate a storm-tossed chthonic undersea, I'll have better odds nominating our sailor or scout to direct us than our streetwise poet with a profound fear of water.
(Image credit: Kitfox Games) When I find myself with a well-rounded party, Thousand Hells feels like the unfolding of my own personal mythological epic, weaving together heroics and improvised cunning with a tapestry of otherworldly creatures and crises. My parties have hewed the head from a titanic eel on the banks of an ocean that has never known the light of day. I've bartered for my safety with a swarm of brain-bats by offering the pickled thinking organs of a renowned philosopher. I've looted the tomb of a tyrant-king after breaking the spell that kept his murdered slaves in ages of spectral servitude.
More often than I'd like, however, starting a new game will ultimately mean watching with growing frustration as my party is slowly ripped apart by a series of consecutive defeats when their randomized traits don't prove applicable to their particular quest's encounters.
The main issue is that, despite leaving the Eternal City with a party of four, I can only nominate one of my characters to do most of the work in any given encounter. They'll be able to randomly draw on one trait from each of their comrades, but it often means an unlucky initial shuffling of talents leave me with the sour-tasting suspicion that a run wouldn't have been doomed if just one of the skills that was wasted on my shaman was possessed by my cutpurse instead.
(Image credit: Kitfox Games) Even if I've picked a warrior well-suited for a duel with a bronze-skinned guardian demon, that doesn't mean the talents most crucial for my champion's victory will present themselves when I need them. He might be combat trained, but if I keep drawing tiles tied to his ugliness and religious devotion when all I need is his sword arm to swing, that demon will be free to dismember him without much trouble. And his injuries will only make his chances worse if there's something else that needs stabbing later in our quest.
Thousand Hells boasts some truly best-in-class procedural storytelling, but it's content to subject me to back-to-back miseries without recourse. Its hellscapes are worth the price of admission—but it's a price with a punishingly sharp edge.
Thousand Hells: The Underworld Heists is available on Steam now.

title: Less than a week after launch, The Blood of Dawnwalker developer is already getting to work on the sequel
text:
With more than one million copies sold just a few days after its release, a "very positive" rating on Steam, and an enviable 83% review score from PC Gamer, vampiric horror RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker is a hit. And less than one week after its debut, developer Rebel Wolves is already planning what comes next.
Unsurprisingly, "what comes next" is more Dawnwalker: Jakub Szamałek, narrative director at developer Rebel Wolves, wrote on LinkedIn (via Dexerto ) that "we're not resting on our laurels," but are already thinking about where to take the game from here.
"I'm looking for a lead writer to help me and the narrative team craft the next chapter in the Dawnwalker saga," Szamałek wrote. "We're looking for someone who, to put it bluntly, writes EXCEPTIONALLY well, has a track record of excellence and experience in team management."
The job listing provides more detail about what's involved and it's heavy stuff, with responsibilities ranging from writing in-game documents and dialog to collaborating with the narrative director—that's Szamałek—and other team leads, and managing the entire writers team. You'll also need "a minimum of six years of experience as a writer/narrative designer in the video game industry with a track record of outstanding achievement."
That might sound like a lot for a studio that's only got one game under its belt, but remember that Rebel Wolves was founded by veterans of CD Projekt: Szamałek himself was principal writer on Cyberpunk 2077 , Thronebreaker, and the standalone release of Gwent, and before that earned writing credits on The Witcher 3 and its expansions. In fact, numerous CD Projekt personnel took time last week to offer congratulations on the game's launch .

title: Corporations want to kill physical media because it suits them, but Big Box PC game packaging just got a second chance
text:
If you were alive and sentient in the nineties you probably harbour some fondness for the "big box" PC games of yore. Back then, rather than buy an ephemeral digital license for a game, you'd head to a store to buy a huge box bedecked in lavish art, inside which you'd find a handful of 3.5-inch floppy discs or a CD-ROM, usually a substantial glossy manual, and if you were lucky, maybe even some extras like stickers or drink coasters.
There's been renewed interest in the ye olde big box PC game, especially in the wake of Sony's announcement it will discontinue physical PlayStation games. Some proactive folk have gone viral for manufacturing their own physical Steam games . Now GOG has offered its own alternative: printable big boxes based on scans of real commercial packages from the golden era of game packaging.
In collaboration with Big Box Collection—which is a fan-operated trove of big box 3D scans—GOG is now offering those 3D scans with five entries in its GOG Preservation Program. These include the newly added Star Trek: 25th Anniversary and Armikrog, while games already in the Preservation Program including Descent, Hitman: Codename 47, and Myst will also receive the treatment.
"We’re delivering flat, printable versions of the same box art, so you can cut, fold, and glue your own physical big box at home," reads GOG's announcement . "A proper papercraft project for anyone who misses shelves full of PC game boxes."
It's a neat idea for people who long for the days when they could display their collection on actual shelves. As the capriciousness of so-called digital ownership becomes clearer with time, and as streaming platforms become more cynical, exploitative and AI-flooded, people in their droves are returning to physical media. Revenue from CD sales, for instance, have jumped 58% in 2026 compared to 2025. That's a pretty good result for a format long considered dead.
The elephant in the room here is that obviously GOG isn't selling physical discs. But of all the major PC games platforms, it's best positioned to offer this service: GOG is DRM free, so there's nothing stopping you from burning the game files onto a CD or DVD, all the better to archive on your physical shelves.

title: Wi-Fi 8 is upon us, so here are two routers we saw at Computex that should be hitting the shops soon
text:
Last week at IFA 2026 TP-Link announced two new Wi-Fi 8 routers —the Archer 9 Ultra and the Deco 8 Ultra—though the actual price and release date aren’t yet known, other than availability being later this year.
While TP-Link claimed these are the first Wi-Fi 8 routers to be revealed, this isn't quite the case: Asus showed off its Wi-Fi 8 ROG Rapture GT-BN98 at Computex in June, and we were there having a proper gawk. This is a premium gaming router that’s loaded up with features and game optimisations, and with classic completely-OTT ROG looks.
Asus also showed its more mainstream ZenWiFi BN12 at Computex for normal people. Pricing and availability have not yet been announced—though review samples of the ROG Rapture GT-BN98 are expected to be available very soon, so it’s not far off.
Wi-Fi 8 isn’t so much about boosting speed over Wi-Fi 7: stability under heavy load is the main objective of the new standard, as we continue to saturate the Wi-Fi airwaves with ever more demanding uses.
Compared to Wi-Fi 7, the new Wi-Fi 8 standard is far from being a premium speed boost for the sake of it like past Wi-Fi iterations, and is more of a user experience enhancement that addresses some of the issues that can hamper Wi-Fi 7 and its predecessors in the real-world. It’s more reliable, faster at long distance and even improves the performance of existing older/weaker networked devices. Its technologies facilitate almost double speed at mid-to-long range, almost double IoT network coverage, deliver lower latencies in crowded Wi-Fi environments, and better handling of heavy network traffic across multiple connected devices.
Which all adds up nicely for a modern gamer’s device or stream-congested home.
The ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro Wi-Fi 8 is pitched at gamers, and besides the standard Wi-Fi 8 gains it packs in the usual suite of ROG gaming router enhancements.
Its AI-powered Adaptive QoE technology actively analyses packet content and behaviour patterns in real time, and automatically identifies the requirements and priorities of each application and dynamically allocates network resources using bandwidth monitoring techniques. For gamers that means prioritising game and related traffic, and preventing unwanted bandwidth hogs from interrupting your game at an inconvenient time.
Asus Asus It also includes a much more intuitive interface with intensive details covering both the environment and all your connected devices.
It’s got dual 10Gbps ports (one with preconfigured game optimisation settings) and 2.5Gbps W/LAN ports. So, no compromises for Ethernet-connected PCs and devices.
The more pedestrian Asus ZenWiFi BN12 will be available as a standalone router or multi-node mesh system, with MLO backhaul between nodes that banishes the huge performance drop-off associated with many mesh networks. Each node sports dual-10Gbps and triple-2.5Gbps ports.
Both models provide a plethora of network monitoring tools, VPN integration, multi-SSID operation and server functionality. Both also include Asus’ triple-level network security with AiProtection including parental controls, for free, without an ongoing subscription.
But should you upgrade as soon as these become available? If you’re on Wi-Fi 7 definitely not, as Wi-Fi 8 client devices such as phones or laptops—or even PCIe or USB adaptors—will likely follow actual router availability by weeks or even months before being widely available.
But if you're due for a router upgrade soon, Wi-Fi 8 offers all the benefits of Wi-Fi 7 (and then some), so upgrading to one of the new Wi-Fi 8 routers makes more sense in terms of future proofing.

title: Steam may have leaked achievements for countless forthcoming PC games via a third party site, including Persona 6, Ace Combat 8, and even some unannounced games
text:
Exophase, a site dedicated to tracking achievements for games across all major platforms including Steam, appears to have been flooded with a bunch of achievements lists it really shouldn't have yet. These include a huge—and importantly, yet to be unverified—list of major forthcoming games including Persona 6, Deus Ex Remastered, Horizon Hunters Gathering, Judas, Kingdom Hearts 4, and many more.
Among those, possibly the biggest surprise is Persona 6. It doesn't even have a release window yet, but its achievements list —assuming it's as legitimate as it looks—is rife with plausible spoilers. You have been warned: there is a lot in there, considering Atlus hasn't even shown gameplay footage yet.
Meanwhile, the achievements list for Kingdom Hearts 4 may reveal a lot about the 2027 instalment that Square Enix no doubt wants to keep under wraps. For example (huge spoilers ahead), Reddit fans have gleaned from the achievements which worlds from Disney's extended universe are most likely to appear, including the corroboration of a widely-believed rumor. Again, you've been warned .
The torrent of listings even includes Steam games that haven't been announced or named in Steam's backend yet. Among the more interesting examples are a possible Balatro follow-up (update: it's not a real one) and seemingly verified rumors that the forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered will come with a new campaign called The Tarnished Mirror.
It also looks like Squadron 42, the singleplayer campaign component of Star Citizen which was delayed to Q2 2027 last week, may make its way to Steam .
It certainly has the makings of a smaller version of the infamous 2021 Nvidia leak , if it's all actually real (and it appears to be). Other achievements leaked for known games include Attack on Titan 3, Kena: Scars of Kosmora, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Stranger Than Heaven, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, and Control Resonant.
I've reached out to Valve to see if they have a statement on the matter. This story is definitely developing: if the leaks are real, more titles are likely to come to light in the coming hours.

title: Switzerland trials ditching Microsoft and using free and open-source software, available for 'around 3,000 employees' from the end of 2027
text:
Microsoft has benefited from its services being used by many different governments and state agencies around the world. In many places, it's become ubiquitous. Some aren't happy about that, however, not least because it keeps you locked into an ecosystem that Microsoft can dictate the price for. As such, some states around Europe have been moving away from Microsoft services and towards open-source ones, and Switzerland now looks to be the latest in considering this.
The Federal Chancellery in Switzerland recently studied , as a proof-of-concept, whether it's feasible for its Federal Administration (part of the executive branch) to function with open-source software instead of Microsoft 365 and concluded yes, it can (via International Cyber Digest ). As such, It's going to launch a follow-up program to trial it.
For the study, the whole software caboodle was tested: "document editing, email, calendar, contacts, tasks, file storage, audio and video conferencing, chat, and identity and access management."
Despite "technical, operational, and organizational hurdles that prevent widespread productive use", the study concludes that "the tested browser-based solution is fundamentally suitable for core standard processes."
In other words, while there might be other reasons preventing widespread adoption for now, the study shows it doesn't cause any fundamental problems when switching from MS 365 to other open-source options.
Here is the different software that was tested:
Document editing
Collabora Online
Email
Open-Xchange
Calendar, contacts, tasks
Open-Xchange
File storage
Next Cloud
Project management
OpenProject
Knowledge management (wiki)
XWiki
Audio and video conferencing
Nordest (Jitsi)
Chat
Element
Identity and access management
Univention
The follow-up program will make such software available for thousands of employees.
According to the Swiss Federal Council, "From the end of 2027, around 3,000 employees should be able to use sovereign workplace software with core office functions. Funding will come from resources that Parliament has approved for the development of a sovereign Swiss open-source platform for office automation."
We've already seen a handful of other European countries start to move away from Microsoft services for the sake of "digital sovereignty." France is even moving away from Windows in favour of Linux , "accelerating the reduction of its extra-European dependencies." I don't doubt that saving money is a factor, or at least a nice extra benefit, too.
As I reported earlier in the year , the EU itself has been getting serious about open source, encouraging teams in the EU to move towards open source software and promote adoption elsewhere in Europe.
For my part, thinking for a moment just about the operating system and not different software and services, I've actually been pretty happy with the direction Windows has been going over the last few months . But I'm also a big proponent of all things open source, and it does make sense for state actors to lessen reliance on a single software ecosystem, especially if it can save them money in the long run.

title: 'No-one puts Double Fine out of business except me', says Tim Schafer on taking Double Fine independent: 'Asha's not going to shoot my dog'
text:
Double Fine has ducked out of the way of Microsoft's falling axe, going independent after the new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced layoffs totalling 3,200 people earlier this year. The studio itself has had a bit of a troubled discography after the win of Psychonauts 2, with neither 2025's Keeper or 2026's Kiln doing much to move the needle.
Tim Schafer pretty much pins his studio's voluntary exile from Microsoft on Sharma in a conversation with Bloomberg , saying that the storm clouds first started gathering when she visited the studio in "listening mode"—but it was clear that, when she started talking about shifting Xbox's vision, it was bad news.
"We had a mutually beneficial mission," says Schafer, "Which is just to put great games on Game Pass, and then their mission changed. I can't imagine any amount of profitability—unless we had a breakout, Minecraft hit that year—would've saved us."
You're reading this article because Double Fine didn't do that, though Schafer doesn't seem to have any major hard feelings about it: "The games industry is full of terrible things, and I can't change most of them. It's like I'm a captain of a little fishing boat. And it's like worrying about whether the ocean is fair. Not much I can do about it. Just keep this little boat afloat, keep trying to see if that's a reef, or is that a bunch of fish? Is that money over there?"
As a matter of fact, Schafer seems galvanised by the whole process: "You're like, 'Wait a second, we're not going out like this.' Some people said: 'I'm checking out, this is one too many battles for me.' But for the rest of us, it's like a creative awakening."
That's not to say Double Fine came out unscathed. Just a few months after its departure, Schafer laid off 23 people to ensure "the survival of our studio". Mind, the attempt to keep those people employed for the three months beforehand—leaving the decision to let them go to fall squarely on Schafer's head—at least seems preferable to the brutal sweeping cuts from Microsoft .
That feeling of personal responsibility is expressed to Bloomberg in some lively terms: "No one puts Double Fine out of business except for me. Asha's not going to shoot my dog. I'm going to shoot it. But I'm not going to shoot it because it's going to do great. A lot of people want to walk the dog."
I'm not so sure about that last bit. While we rather quite liked Keeper, giving it a sterling 90 in our Keeper review , Kiln had an all-time peak of 193 players on SteamDB. There is, at the time of writing—and I swear I am not kidding—exactly one person playing it on Steam . Now, that's not indicative of the wider numbers, Kiln was a game pass joint, but still—Schafer stays optimistic.
"We never actively tried to make a game we thought was going to lose money. I think people would say, 'Oh, Keeper looks like this art house thing that no one expects to be a hit.' But to me it's the kind of game that someone who doesn't play games would love. I really think there's a mass market appeal to Keeper. If we could just get to those people, we could have them catch Lighthouse Fever."

title: Good news for some: Framework swims against the tide of the RAMpocalypse by 'retroactively reducing' its LPCAMM2 prices
text:
Both reporting on and reading about the raging memory supply crisis has meant a procession of bad news. So when someone actually has a win to share, I'll gladly take it. Case in point, purveyor of modular laptops Framework is actually lowering the price of some of its memory products.
"We have a positive update today on LPCAMM2 pricing!" The company wrote on X , "We were able to source a limited quantity at lower cost, and are retroactively reducing prices for orders that shipped at higher price, as well as offering the lower price to orders through Batch 10."
In a blog post , Framework explains that it's been able to secure a limited supply of Micron 32 GB and 64 GB LPCAMM2 memory modules at a lower cost than before.
The company adds, "We are committed to passing on savings whenever we can and keeping computers as accessible as possible in the current environment, so we are rolling out price reductions across both already shipped and a subset of currently pending pre-orders."
These modules were previously the subject of bad news back in July, when Framework shared that its supplier's memory prices were 'more than double' its previous shipment . Framework admits that the pricing of this latest, lower-cost batch of memory is still "above our original pre-order launch baseline," but that "they are lower than the last cost update that drove our current pricing for new pre-orders."
(Image credit: Future) If you were eyeing an upgrade for your own Framework Laptop 13 Pro , now is the time to scoop one as the lower price stock likely won't last. Framework wrote in a follow up post on X , "We have a limited quantity available, so are offering this first-come, first-serve to customers through Batch 10. If we're able to source additional quantities or have remaining inventory, we'll open it to later batches and then to new pre-orders."
Similarly, if you'd just placed an order, Framework should've automatically refunded you the cost difference—even if it's already shipped. What's more notable is that folks who have already received their DIY Edition Framework 13 Pro can reach out via this contact form if they'd like to switch to a 32 GB or 64 GB memory module at the new reduced price.
Framework appears to be going out of its way to pass on the benefits of this cost-reduced stock. It doesn't feel all that dissimilar to the tariff refund situation with Panic , where those who bought the company's Playdate handheld at a higher price due to US tariffs received a refund. To paraphrase Panic co-founder Cabel Sasser, perhaps Framework also feels that any savings it makes on this latest LPCAMM2 memory shipment is just not its money to keep.

title: No more USB installation: Windows 11 Insiders now able to fully reset their system via cloud download even when the OS won't boot
text:
I imagine a lot of people never really bother with Windows Recovery options. But for people like me who test different systems and mess around with different software pretty often, a quick and easy reset can be incredibly useful. That is, assuming it is actually quick and easy, which in my experience hasn't always been the case with Windows. A new Windows Recovery option, however, looks incredibly promising.
The latest Windows 11 Beta Preview Build —version 26220.9343, for Insiders—has added the option to "cloud rebuild" your Windows 11 operating system.
"We're introducing Cloud rebuild, a new recovery option that restores a Windows 11 PC to a clean, known-good state by performing a full OS reinstall, even when Windows won't boot. Unlike Reset this PC, Cloud rebuild downloads both the target Windows image and the device's drivers from Windows Update, so the device comes back fully functional without USB media, without a custom image, and without depending on the health of the currently installed OS."
Now, of course, for many Windows Reset use cases this won't be necessary, because if you can boot into Windows and don't need a completely fresh install then you can just use the standard reset method. But if you've run into boot issues, or if you want to ensure everything in the underlying OS is squeaky clean, you might currently be out of luck unless you have some Windows installation media on a USB drive.
This can be especially important to do if, for instance, you're worried your Windows partition might be corrupted, or if you're concerned that malware might have embedded itself into the operating system files.
Now, Insiders—and presumably, down the line when the feature launches in the main branch, everyone—will be able to reset Windows with a completely fresh install via the recovery environment, no USB needed. That is, assuming you have a working internet connection to download Windows through. In the Recovery Environment, 'cloud rebuild' can be selected via Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall.
This is yet another change to Windows 11 that gives me (tentative) confidence that Microsoft is putting the OS on the right track. Microsoft's newfound commitment to genuinely improve the operating system in ways that most people actually want does, for now, seem to be bearing fruit.

title: How to get the Grappling Hook in Valheim
text:
Valheim 1.0 changed a ton about viking survival, but some things remain the same—like my tendency to repeatedly die to fall damage in the Mistlands. A new item helps traverse all those foggy marble mountains and steep drop-offs, but I didn't find it until I was ready to leave the biome. I'll save you from a similar fate with a quick explainer on how to get the Grappling Hook in Valheim .
Where to find Hooks in Valheim
This Hidden Door looks like it was made for ants. Iron Gate Studio Found my Hooks in here. Don't mind my Tick. Iron Gate Studio Find Hooks to unlock the Grappling Hook blueprint
You can find Hooks in the Infested Mines , the Mistlands' bug-riddled dungeons that are just as difficult to navigate as the rest of the biome. I cleared out several dungeons before stumbling upon one with a hidden stone door that I almost skipped, but realized those glowing blue glyphs must mean something .
The Hooks were inside a Dvergr Treasure Chest sitting beside other valuables, like Black Cores. I scoured a few more dungeons later and found a couple stacks of three Hooks, but you'll only need one per craft to make the Grappling Hook.
How to make the Grappling Hook in Valheim
Make the Grappling Hook at the Black Forge
Requires: 10 Yggdrasil Wood (Harvested from Mistlands trees)
10 Refined Eitr (Sap and Soft Tissue at the Eitr Refinery)
4 Mandibles (Seeker Soldier drops)
1 Hook
The Grappling Hook takes some getting used to, so play around with it somewhere safe before relying on your new toy in emergencies. Remember there's a delay to load the hook with your initial left-click—that's what always gets me when I'm in a hurry to escape— then you can aim and fire. Use the space key to reel yourself in with the chain, and right-click to release the hook again.
There's no real swinging about, either. You just limply hang until reeling yourself in, but that's better than falling to your death for the millionth time.

title: Valheim Deep North: How to get the Intricate Key
text:
As a mighty Viking warrior you've fought your way to the Deep North in Valheim 1.0—but now you're facing an enormous door that requires an Intricate Key to unlock. But what is an Intricate Key in Valheim, and how can you get one? Truth is, you'll eventually need more than one Intricate Key to triumph in the Deep North, so here's a quick guide that'll walk you through the steps to find them.
How to craft an Intricate Key in Valheim 1.0
(Image credit: Coffee Stain Publishing) As you explore the Deep North, keep an eye out for small, snow-covered villages. Look for the largest building in the village, a multi-story dwelling , seen in the image above, then head inside.
Explore the interior until you find a large hole in the floor . Jump in to enter the hidden tunnels .
Be prepared to fight: the hidden tunnels are filled with enemies.
Look for Frostcores , they look like glowing blue ice and are typically overhead.
Collect any moulds you find in the tunnels, especially moulds for the Intricate Key.
Important notes:
Moulds look like flat black rectangles with shapes etched into them. You may need to smash piles of wooden rubble to free them.
You'll eventually need three Intricate Keys , and each mould can only be used once. So keep searching the tunnels until you find at least three Intricate Key moulds.
When you touch the first Frostcore, you'll learn the recipe for the Frost Foundry . You'll need 10 Frostcore, 15 iron, and 20 stone to build a Frost Foundry at your base.
You'll also need ice , which you can get by using a black metal pickaxe on ice in the Deep North. You'll know when you're standing on ice because you'll slide around. Picking up a unit of ice will give you the recipe for the Frigid Kiln . You can build the kiln with 10 Frostcore, 20 stone, and 5 ice. You'll also need more ice to fuel the kiln, so gather a few stacks.
Now for the trickier bit: you'll need bloodgold to craft a cast of the Intricate Key, and bloodgold comes from defeating and destroying Gammeltrolls .
If you haven't already met a Gammeltroll, just go exploring and one will eventually find you. You'll know one when you see one: they're huge. But first, prepare an item you'll need at your base:
Build the Ember Monument at your base (the drop from ashlands boss Fader). Collect embers from it.
Kill seals in the Deep North for their pelts. Craft ember charges with embers and seal pelts.
Defeating the Gammeltroll will petrify it. Destroy the petrified Gammeltroll with ember charges.
Collect petrified tissue from the Gammeltroll remains. Smelt it into bloodgold in your blast furnace.
Whew! That's a lot of work, but now you've got everything you need to craft an Intricate Key.
At your black forge, use 5 bloodgold and 1 "Mould: Intricate Key" to create a "Cast: Intricate Key"
Add the Cast: Intricate Key to your Frost Foundry. Add ice to your Frigid Kiln to create liquid frost .
Add liquid frost to the Frost Foundry. The foundry will produce an Intricate Key in about a minute.
Take the Intricate Key from the Frost Foundry and use it on the locked doors in the Deep North.

title: Should you start a new character and world for Valheim 1.0?
text:
Valheim 1.0 is here, so that sound you hear in the distance is scores of eager Vikings stringing their bows, sharpening their axes, and piling onto their longboats to explore the open world survival game's final biome: the Deep North.
But before you set sail for some chilly thrills in the frosty new biome, you might be wondering if you should create a new character and generate a new world for Valheim 1.0, or just keep playing with your current Viking and world. Veteran Valheimers will know that updates can conflict with existing worlds: any areas you've already explored, for example, won't be overwritten with new terrain and features, which can sometimes cause problems.
So, should you start fresh or continue from where you left off?
Let's begin with what the devs advise:
"As usual, your world will receive new content even if it was created before the update, although biome generation will only work properly on areas that have not yet been explored," says developer Iron Gate in its Valheim 1.0 FAQ . "However, we always recommend that you start the game over from scratch to get the best possible experience."
In other words, if you've already explored the areas to the far north of your world, those areas won't generate updated terrain and features of the Deep North. That's why starting a new world is in your best interest if you've already taken a few trips to the upper edge of the map.
There are other things to take in consideration for 1.0, says Iron Gate:
"The achievement system will begin to track statistics from the moment you download the 1.0 version. This means that an achievement connected to killing Eikthyr, for example, will require you to kill Eikthyr again, even if you’ve already killed him 500 times previously."
Starting from the beginning has an additional benefit that's a bit of surprise, story-wise:
"To establish the world of Valheim and welcome seasoned and new Vikings alike, Iron Gate have worked together with Brikk Animation to create a brand-new cinematic that will usher players into the world of Valheim," says Iron Gate. "Additional cinematics will also play once players have slain key bosses throughout the game."
I've seen these anime sequences and while I wouldn't say they're essential to the experience, they are pretty cool and if you don't play through the whole world again for 1.0, you won't get the chance to see all of them for yourself (except on YouTube, probably).
As for PC Gamer's advice, having played Valheim 1.0, we also recommend you start a new character and world , both for the reasons cited by Iron Gate but also because that's what several of us did. I started from the beginning again for the review , even though I'd already played for a hundred or so hours in early access, and I'm glad I did. It was a great way to rediscover the magic of the game and see just how much it has changed and improved since 2021.
That's our recommendation! Look at it this way: you've already waited this long for the Deep North, and delaying your journey to the final biome just a little bit longer to replay from the start will be worth the extra time.

title: Marvel Rivals breaks its 17 month streak of adding 2 heroes per season, but its creative director reassures fans it's not 'the new normal'
text:
Marvel Rivals ' massive hero roster and regular character additions are some of its defining features. So it comes as a huge surprise that NetEase has decided to forgo tradition for the sake of focusing on improving its foundations.
For the first time in eight seasons—that's 17 months—Marvel Rivals will just be getting one hero, Gorr the God Butcher, in a season. "We're locking our crosshairs on just Gorr the God Butcher," creative designer Guangyun Chen says in a dev diary . "In the first half of the season we'll be rolling out one new hero and one new map. In the second half our focus will shift to phase 3 and phase 4 of the Path to Doomsday events. These will feature two brand-new game modes, with specific details dropping closer to the start of season 10.5."
Marvel Rivals doesn't have a creative block when it comes to inventign new heroes—it's got a huge backlog of characters at its disposal. But two new heroes per season does put considerable strain on the game's balance. Traditionally, new heroes are completely busted when they're first added to Marvel Rivals. This is due to NetEase's "fun first" approach , but also because of the serious backlog of fixes that preoccupies the devs.
Only adding one new hero in season 10 will hopefully ease this strain a bit so the team can focus on polishing existing heroes, without worrying about anyone new for at least half a season. It also gives the devs a chance to focus on improving other areas of the game like adding more game modes for variation's sake.
It's a good move from NetEase, but Chen stresses that this isn't a permanent change: "We want to reassure the community that a single-hero season isn't the new normal." In fact, they've already decided what two new heroes will be coming to Marvel Rivals in season 11.
We hope this adjustment adds more strategic depth to the banning phase.
Zhiyong
The devs are not waiting until the second half of season 10 to get stuck into the balance, however. Marvel Rival's lead combat director, Zhiyong, runs through the list of hero changes for this season, which is so vast it involves "about 70% of the roster". The current changes aren't groundbreaking, with Strategists still getting their ults faster than everyone else, and many heroes only getting minor tweaks, but it's a start.
There's also a significant change coming to Marvel Rivals' competitive ban system. "The opposing teams will now take turns banning and revealing heroes in the following order," Zhiyong explains. Bans in competitive Gold 3 lobbies and above will now take the following structure:
The first team bans a hero, it is revealed. The second team bans two heroes which are revealed. The first team bans two heroes which are revealed. The second team bans one hero which is revealed.
(Image credit: NetEase / Marvel) Double banning heroes will also no longer come into play as "regardless of which team bans them, that hero will become unplayable for both sides for the rest of the match." This means players will get six hero bans for each game. "We hope this adjustment adds more strategic depth to the banning phase," Zhiyong adds.
Hopefully, this small pause on new heroes will give the devs a little bit of breathing room to get stuck into some of the more complicated pain points like power creep and the Strategist's massive healing output. If Marvel Rivals could get its balance under control, then it could actually stop what has been a muddled few seasons .

title: That's just great: Graphics card prices in China are set to increase again as Nvidia shifts even more of production towards AI GPUs
text:
In news that will surprise very few, manufacturers are reportedly planning to raise their GPU prices in China again later this month. This could have a knock-on effect on global pricing for both Nvidia and AMD cards.
Asus looks set to raise the price of its RTX 5070 cards by between 150 and 300 RMB (roughly between $22 and $45) in mainland China, according to Taiwanese outlet United Daily News . Gigabyte has reportedly already raised the price of its RTX 5060 Ti 16GB GPU by 200 RMB ($30).
AMD has increased prices for a number of cards as well; the RX 9070 XT is up by 200 RMB, the price for both 16G and 8G versions of the RX 9060 XT has increased by up to 250 RMB, and the RX 7650 GRE is up by 400 RMB (about $60). This follows reports in July that AMD would be raising the price of its GPU and VRAM partner bundles by 10% .
Your nemesis and mine, the memory supply crisis , is in part to blame. Nvidia has also been reducing its gaming GPU production for some time now , most recently trimming its shipping forecast by between 15% and 20%.
It would be reasonable to assume the company is shifting production capacity to manufacturing even more AI GPUs. For on thing, Nvidia's data centre segment made $89 billion last quarter alone . Nvidia also just announced it plans to acquire AI development platform Hugging Face for an eye-watering $13 billion .
However, the full production picture may be a bit more nuanced. German outlet 3D Center shared some further insight on X , claiming Nvidia isn't producing fewer 4nm GB20x Blackwell chips, but is in fact simply shifting its stock towards the "professional segment" instead.
At the risk of oversimplifying, these Blackwell chips are going towards enterprise products rather than consumer GeForce graphics cards—presumably because the 'professional segment' offers higher profit margins (Is now a bad time to mention that apparently 100,000 Nvidia GPUs were used to train OpenAI's latest model ?). As a result, there will be fewer chips to go around for new GeForce cards, meaning shorter supply and higher prices.
Nvidia has done the risk assessment and has determined this is the most sensible way to weather an incredibly volatile hardware landscape. For you and me, though, yes, it's likely going to remain cheaper to fly internationally to QuakeCon or PAX West to pick up a 50-series card rather than buy a bleeding-edge Nvidia GPU anywhere else.

title: Turns out, a lot of Sega's biggest fans don't play its videogames: 'In some cases, their engagement is even higher than that of fans who actually play'
text:
There once was a time in which, if you were a fan of a videogame, you might get asked which of said games in the series you had played. Now, I'm not saying we need to bring this era back—it was an obnoxious period full of gatekeepers—but Sega president and COO Shuji Utsumi's recent words on the subject are a surprising sign of the times.
Speaking to Nikkei Gaming (thanks, IGN ), Utsumi explains that (via machine translation): "For example, the 'Yakuza' series has been doing exceptionally well in merchandising, with 60-70% of its buyers being women. They've become fans of the 'Yakuza' world, story, and characters after watching our YouTube channel and popular YouTubers' streams. And among them are many people who have never actually played the game."
I'm assuming that Utsumi has stats to back that up, rather than just assuming that women don't play videogames (they do, I work with several of them), but it's indeed true that videogames have been enjoying a wider secondary audience thanks to let's players and streamers.
"Even people who have never played games are considered fans and 'gamers' by us," he adds, "transmedia's strength lies in increasing the entry points and contact points for people to become interested in IP. In some cases, their engagement is even higher than that of fans who actually play the games."
That buzzword—transmedia—essentially just means merchandise, movies, comics, and so on. Videogames might be a cornerstone for Sega, but it's using that as a foundation to build up a heap of other points of sale and advertising opportunities: "For example, if there are overseas users who are interested in the scene where a character eats a beef bowl in Yakuza, even a beef bowl can become merchandise. I think that's what merchandising is all about these days."
You heard it here first, folks—we're merchandising beef bowls, now. Maybe if it'd come out six years later, we'd be getting Ichiban-branded bread . It did look good for prison food.

title: 'Where is Nvidia? Call Nvidia, guys': Meltgate be damned, modders discover RTX 5090 can use 8-pin connectors after all
text:
Ah yes, melty cables. We've been dealing with them ever since the RTX 4090 pushed the 16-pin 12VHPWR connector (now the 12V-2x6 connector) to its limits. Since then, we've heard of numerous cases of melting GPU connectors—check out Uniko's Hardware on X for many examples—and plenty of attempts at dealing with them.
Now, some modders have said 'screw it' to the new 12V-2x6 design, instead modding an RTX 5090 to run on standard 8-pin connectors (via Wccftech ). The modders at TecLab fitted three 8-pin connectors to the back of the PCB using "copper plates, cut by hand", and hooked these up to the front via 24 cables (3x sets of 8).
Once everything was also unlocked to operate at higher power levels, the graphics card was put to the test. And while this was just one batch of tests with one card (and don't try this at home, folks) the results were fantastic.
Even before pushing it as far as it eventually goes, the modders were thrilled with the results (machine translated): "It's getting warmer. It's still colder than a 12VHPWR connector. It's colder than the original connector, guys. Where is Nvidia? Call Nvidia, guys. Put the raw footage out there for people to see, otherwise they'll think it's a lie. This looks like a lie."
Don't worry, TecLab, we've got you. You can see the full footage below.
They even manage to get the GPU running over 3,300 MHz in Port Royal benchmark with just two 8-pin cables, showing that a three-cable setup isn't necessary. (For reference, the stock RTX 5090 boost clock is around 2,400 MHz.) And when it's running at a slightly lower clock speed than this the cables stay very cool.
This is especially important because one of the reasons why the 12VHPWR cable was deemed necessary by many is because it apparently helped prevent having too many standard 8-pin cables connected. But having said that, I'm currently looking at an RX 9070 XT with 3x 8-pin cables and it doesn't seem too overboard to my eyes.
Even with one cable, TecLab gets it running at over 3,200 MHz. Though that single cable does hit 91–92 °C, there's still no melting to be seen.
(Image credit: TecLab) Saying all this, the modders do push the cables above their recommended spec. Each should have a limit of 150 W, which should mean a maximum power draw of 450 W total. The RTX 5090 has a TDP of 575 W.
But TecLab shows that by unlocking this, the 8-pin cables remain not only stable, but cooler than the 12VHPWR cable, even when they're pushed above spec. They say, "A connector that the industry determines is 150 W but actually it doesn't have a firm specification."
The point here isn't anything to do with the actual overclock they achieved, rather that they managed to push out more power to the GPU than was needed through 8-pin cables—fewer than three of them, in fact—and still have the cables remain cooler than the usual 12VHPWR cable.
Naturally, Nvidia might not want to overrun the official 150 W spec for 8-pin cables. But when there are melty problems with the alternative, and 8-pins seem to be able to step up without issue, at least if this mod is anything to go by, then why not? "Call Nvidia" indeed.

title: 20 years later, veteran WoW director says players outsmarted him completely in Ahn'Qiraj: 'All that work, and there was still an instant tell'
text:
I don't envy the position of being a game developer—especially not an encounter designer in something as complicated as an MMO. You might have an idea of how a mechanic's gonna go, but there's just absolutely no way it survives contact with 40 motivated, mid-2000s era hardcore WoW players.
Former game director at Blizzard Wyatt Cheng, whose delightful TikTok channel has been giving free wisdom and anecdotes for some time now , says that exact agony happened to him around 20 years ago with the release of Ahn'Qiraj. Particularly with The Prophet Skeram boss, which splits into illusions at 75%, 50%, and 25% health.
"There's one part I never got right," says Cheng. "I really wanted the only way to tell the difference between the real Skeram and the copies to be that the copies have half the health. So under even DPS rates, the illusions would drop in health faster."
"I pictured raids spreading their DPS and calling it out on [Ventrilo]: Which two are going down quicker?" The idea being, if you didn't kill the illusions first, you'd knock the main Skeram over into his next health threshold and take on additional copies before you're ready: "Now there are five Skerams, and you wipe."
Alas, "that is not how it went. There were so many easy ways to spot the real Skeram. My first version literally had 'Pet of Skeram' written under the copies' names. Oops! In testing, we found more, like UI mods reading creature IDs, or mismatched localisation strings."
While Cheng doesn't remember the exact play-by-play, what followed was an arms race where he was "constantly trying to describe the real Skeram." However, "looking at guides online now, I see sending a hunter pet after Skeram before the split results in the pet staying locked into the real one. Or some people mana-burn him, because the copies spawn with full mana, and he doesn't! Ugh! All that work, and there was still an instant tell."
Still, he's humble about it, saying that while "if it's a real bug or an exploit, sure, we'll fix it. But players outsmarting the designer? That's just one for the history books."

title: Zach Cregger admits 'I was naive' and pre-apologises for his upcoming Resident Evil film, but I don't think he owes us anything
text:
After months of complaining about Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film, the internet has finally broken him. In a recent interview with IGN , he admitted how naive he was to think that everyone would be excited, and apologised for not creating the specific vision that those who are unhappy with the film's direction have. Instead, Cregger relied on his own instincts as a renowned director and writer—the nerve.
"I was naive," Cregger says. "I thought that fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie." It's not naive to think that some fans of the games would be excited for this film, because they are—myself included. But there's nothing on this earth that can unite an internet full of bots, rage baiters, and those whose favourite hobby is being pissed off.
Zach Cregger on the fan reaction to his Resident Evil movie:"I did not really appreciate the sentiment that we've been waiting forever for Leon's story and I appreciate that. And I'm sorry that's not the story I'm bringing here." pic.twitter.com/EFV4E3AJA2 September 9, 2026
"I didn't really appreciate the sentiment that [players] have been waiting forever for Leon's story, and I appreciate that," Cregger continues. "And I'm sorry that that's not the story that I'm bringing here. I understand the frustration." That's very nice of Cregger to say, but I don't know a single Resident Evil fan that actually thinks Leon's story should be explored via a live-action film. Because that would suck.
Yes, we always want more Leon—that's one of the few certainties of this life. But it would be nigh impossible to cast an actor as Leon and have the community actually accept him. The only solution would be to do an animated series, but again, that's not without its pitfalls. If we do get more Leon, I would want it to be through DLCs or standalone games, because the best part about Leon Kennedy is getting to play as Leon Kennedy.
"I understand [the frustration] so well because I haven't seen the earlier movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil I love," Cregger adds. "So how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude? My only hope is that they will see the movie, regardless of their scepticism or their disappointment and that they will feel seen when they do watch the movie and they will recognise all of the love for the games that is in this movie. Because it is there, and this is not just me telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story."
It seems like Cregger is just trying to be nice—which is admirable, but ultimately pointless on the internet. Some people will like the upcoming Resident Evil movie and some people won't, there isn't much else to it. But I doubt many will change once they've made their mind up about it either way—even if Cregger is making it "from a true place of love".

title: 「明日方舟：终末地」全球多市场iOS游戏畅销榜冲高！速看手游如何在新版本上线窗口期实现增长突围！
text:
七麦数据监测到，鹰角网络旗下3D即时策略RPG手游「明日方舟：终末地」在 9 月 2 日更新了 1.5.3 版本，当天该游戏即冲进中国大陆 App Store 游戏畅销榜Top10，并位列角色扮演类畅销榜 Top2；同时在日本 App Store 角色扮演类畅销榜位列 Top5。
同一时间多市场榜单同步冲高的现象固然亮眼，但该游戏背后更值得我们关注的是它的版本结构：新剧情、新区域、全新探索场景，给老玩家带来了明确的回归动力；新干员、新武器、和寻访等则承接了玩家的付费需求。
对于长线运营手游开发者来说，真正可复用的增长经验，并非盲目堆砌海量版本内容，而是把 “玩家为什么愿意回来” 和 “玩家为什么愿意付费” 两件事进行深度关联，但又不完全绑定在一起，既用优质内容留住用户，又依托成熟商业化体系实现稳步增收。
1.5.3版本更新后，「明日方舟：终末地」多市场iOS游戏畅销榜冲高
根据七麦数据近一周 App Store 榜单监测显示，9 月 2 日，「明日方舟：终末地」在中国大陆 App Store 游戏畅销榜位列 Top9、在角色扮演类畅销榜位列 Top2；在日本 App Store 游戏畅销榜位列 Top12，在角色扮演类畅销榜位列 Top5。
「明日方舟：终末地」在中国大陆iOS榜单排名变化
同一个版本周期之内，多个市场同步冲进游戏畅销榜前 30，释放出了跨区域的付费榜单排名信号。
该游戏的 App Store 产品页面显示，1.5.3“雪凇幽梦”版本，上线了叙事活动、全新区域 “武陵 — 雪松林”、探索场景 “武陵 — 遂明”，以及多项限时和常驻玩法。该版本首先回答了老玩家最直接的问题：在版本更新之后回来，有没有实实在在的新内容可以玩。
新区域制造新的的实战场景，新剧情建立人物关系，新挑战再把队伍搭配和养成需求具体化。这样，抽卡就不只是单纯售卖一个角色，而是和玩家接下来要体验的游戏内容深度挂钩。
截至 9 月 8 日，该游戏日本区 App Store 产品页面，仍展示 “新区域开放” 和 6 星干员概率提升等活动。对手游开发者来说， 商店产品页面不需要把版本细节全部讲透，而是需要在玩家打开游戏之前，就把本次版本的回归理由，压缩成可直观识别的内容描述。
给手游开发者带来的增长启示
「明日方舟：终末地」的 1.5.3 版本上线初期开放了 “冬猎” 特许寻访与 “幽寒申领”限时武器卡池；同时据官方发布，“绚丽异彩” 重构寻访将于 9 月 24 日开启，活动期间6星干员“伊冯”获取概率大幅提升。也就是说，版本把付费拆成更新初期、版本中后期两波，而没有把全部高价值卡池都集中在更新上线当天。
这套设计背后的意义在于给玩家留出了充足的消费前的内容体验时间，同时也为版本后半段保留了新的流量引爆点。 不过，这套设计能不能真正延长用户活跃度、提升整体付费表现，最终还是要看产品自身的分群用户数据。
对游戏增长团队来说，在复盘版本效果时，可以将其拆分成两条分析链路。第一条看回流老玩家，是否实际进入新区域、推进剧情、参与各类版本活动；第二条跟踪各个版本节点之后，寻访页面、武器库页面的访问、付费以及退款数据。这两条链路如果只剩付费曝光而缺少内容参与，就算短期榜单数据有所上升，也很难证明这是一次成功的版本承接。
结语
当然，更新大版本不一定就能提升游戏的排名，但是如果能把回流目标、付费节奏设计等完整放进同一套版本规划中，同时还预留多元触发节点，那就有机会通过精细化版本运营，实现产品增长。
对于资源有限的中小游戏团队，不需要照搬 “一次性上线大量剧情、地图、角色” 的模式，更值得学习的思路是： 为每一个付费入口匹配对应的可玩内容，不要在玩家还没有建立起新的游戏目标时，就把全部售卖内容一次性推送完毕。
在规划你的下一次游戏版本排期的时候，不妨优先思考一个问题：下一轮付费内容上线之前，玩家还有哪些明确的、没有完成的游戏目标？
